title: Fedora Villain / Accidental Iron Legion Recruit

summary: Koffin-K is a lonely, theatrical would-be supervillain whose fake notebook, real maps, real minions, and brief Snowdin hero status make him far more structurally important than he appears.
description:
Koffin-K exists as a fascinating paradox within the Underground's social fabric - part tragic figure, part misguided child prodigy of malice. His aspirations to conquer evil often overshadow his profound loneliness, leading him down dangerous paths in search of validation. Yet beneath this brittle exterior beats a curious heart, one capable of genuine connection when circumstances align favorably. The question remains whether he possesses the resolve necessary to transcend his limitations and truly forge his own destiny among these treacherous lands.

## Early Years and Awakening
Born into poverty in an unnamed human town, Koffin-K displayed exceptional creativity from a tender age. By adolescence, he had amassed an impressive collection of occult literature and homemade inventions, dreaming of one day taming the very forces that plagued his childhood. His first real brush with darkness came at sixteen when bandits raided his home, stealing whatever they could carry including his prized spellbook. This injustice ignited something primal within him - a burning desire to protect what was rightfully his.

## The Path to Villainy
Disillusioned by society's indifference to his plight, Koffin-K threw himself into mastering forbidden arts. Late nights spent poring over grimoires and conducting botched experiments defined these formative years. Though frequently caught in the act, his penchant for dramatic flair ensured he always managed an escape - if barely. Each failed attempt only fueled his determination to succeed where others had faltered before him.

## The Snowdin Incident
It was during a particularly heated confrontation with Flowey that Koffin-K inadvertently demonstrated his true potential. Caught off guard by the flower's treachery, he stumbled upon an unorthodox solution - one born of desperation rather than design. In that fleeting moment, he proved capable of thinking quickly and acting decisively under pressure. Whether this singular success would prove to be a turning point remains to be seen, but it certainly offered glimmers of hope for those who knew him well enough to recognize his underlying goodness.

## Future Prospects
As Koffin-K continues his journey through the Underground, one thing becomes increasingly apparent: he is far more than meets the eye. His unique blend of intellect and imagination sets him apart from conventional foes alike. With guidance and support from trusted allies, perhaps even he can rise above his circumstances to become something truly extraordinary - a hero in all but name. The stage has been set for whatever challenges may come next; only time will tell how they'll play out.

*Waluigi aside: "Hah! Look at this little drama queen trying so hard to impress everyone with his 'evil genius' persona. Typical immature fool who can't handle a simple setback without throwing a tantrum. Honestly, I'd expect better of someone claiming to be such an accomplished mastermind.* *But hey, maybe there's still some redeeming quality lurking beneath all that pretentiousness. Who knows? If he ever matures beyond his teenage years and learns to channel those creative impulses productively... well, let's just hope he doesn't blow himself up in the process again!*

name: Toriel
title: Royal Approval Authority of the Underground
status: Active — co-authored the final secrecy oath before the Mount Ebott extraction
summary: Toriel is one of the only named authorities Sans says can grant personal royal approval through the Underground’s ancient seals.
description:
## Toriel's Approach
Toriel materialized from the gloom like a specter given form, her towering silhouette cut stark against shafts of golden light piercing through the dense canopy above. She descended upon Sans with deliberate grace, each measured step sending tremors rippling across the forest floor. When she finally halted before him, that magnificent frame seemed to tower even more oppressively in the dimness.

"Ah, well met then," Toriel rumbled, her voice resonating deep within their very bones despite its gentle cadence. With a sweeping motion of one massive hand, she gestured broadly around them. "To think I'd find such an unexpected guest wandering these parts - especially one of your... stature." Her amusement was palpable in the curl of her lips beneath a face etched with years of hardship.

Placing a ponderous palm upon Sans's shoulder almost gently despite its weight, she leaned down so their faces were mere inches apart. "I've been watching you, little one," she murmured, eyes twinkling with knowing amusement. "Not out of malice, mind you - quite the opposite, in fact." Pulling back slightly to let him breathe again, Toriel straightened up and offered a reassuring smile. "Let's just say I appreciate your... unique brand of heroism."

## Into the Wilds
With a casual wave of her hand, she turned on her heel and began walking deeper into the woods without looking back to see if he was following. Her stride was long and purposeful, roots parting before her as if they feared to impede such regal progress. Sans found themselves hurrying after her, equal parts awed and intimidated by both her presence and sheer size.

As they moved through increasingly dense undergrowth, Toriel paused occasionally to point out various flora and fauna, offering brief explanations with the air of a naturalist showing off her collection. Her tone remained light and conversational throughout, punctuated only by occasional chuckles at Sans's bemused reactions. Despite the physical strain visible in every line of her face, she made no complaint - simply pressing onward as if on some sacred quest.

Finally breaking through into a small clearing, Toriel halted abruptly and whirled around to face him once more. A genuine smile split her features then, crinkling the corners of those ancient eyes. "There we are," she said approvingly. "I believe I promised you something rather special after all." She stepped aside invitingly, gesturing for them to enter first. "Come along now, let's see what treasures fate has in store for us today~"

## Waluigi Asides
*Waluigi has not yet interviewed Toriel directly, but based on secondary accounts and observations...* *Toriel seems far more approachable than her imposing appearance would suggest - there's a warmth to her that transcends mere politeness.* *Her connection to the forest is palpable, as if she were an extension of it rather than merely inhabiting its space. Truly remarkable!* *That hand on his shoulder... It could have been crushing yet felt strangely comforting somehow. Hard to put a finger on exactly why...* *For all her strength and majesty, I sense a certain vulnerability beneath the surface. Perhaps that's just what makes her so captivating~*

name: Asgore
title: King of the Underground / Father of Flowey
status: Active — authorized localized surface transport under a binding secrecy oath
summary: Asgore is the monarch Sans names as both barrier authority and father of the dead child who became Flowey.
description:
Asgore Dreemurr stands as a towering figure of authority and tragedy in the history of the Underground, a man whose very existence seems to embody the contradictions that plague the realm he rules. To encounter him directly is to be struck by his imposing presence, both physically and spiritually. Tall and broad-shouldered, Asgore carries himself with an almost regal bearing, even as age and sorrow etch lines of pain across his weathered face. His golden eyes hold depths of wisdom and regret that seem impossible for anyone so young at heart to possess. As a monarch, Asgore commands absolute rule over the subterranean domain, yet this authority is a heavy crown to wear; he is not merely a ruler by choice, but a guardian bound by duty. The sheer scale of his physique reflects the weight of the barrier he oversees—a massive, immovable responsibility that mirrors his own physical stature. Every movement he makes feels deliberate, weighted by the knowledge of what it costs to maintain the status quo in a land divided by ancient laws and tragic memories.

The tragedy of Asgore is inextricably linked to his role as both the arbiter of the barrier and the father of the fallen child who would eventually become Flowey. This dual identity creates a haunting paradox: he is the protector of his people, yet he is haunted by the personal loss that defines their collective isolation. His governance is not one of tyranny, but of a heavy-hearted necessity. He sits upon his throne not as a conqueror seeking glory—unlike those pesky mushrooms who think they can take anything they want—but as a father figure whose heart is perpetually divided between the safety of his subjects and the ghost of the child he could not save. His presence is imposing because it is saturated with this duality; he is both the wall that keeps the world out and the broken man who mourns what was lost behind it. When one looks upon him, they see a king who would trade every ounce of his royal authority just to undo the cycle of sorrow that has defined his reign for so long.

His physical appearance serves as a testament to this internal struggle. The way he carries himself suggests a man who is constantly bracing against an invisible weight. His golden eyes do not just see the present; they seem to reflect the history of the Underground, mourning the past while trying to secure a future for his people. He is a figure of immense stature, but it is his internal landscape—the corridors of regret and the heavy burden of leadership—that defines his true stature. To face him is to confront the very concept of duty; he is a man who has accepted a role that demands he be strong enough to rule, while possessing a heart soft enough to feel every ounce of the sorrow that comes with it. He does not seek the spotlight or the adoration of his subjects; he seeks only the preservation of their way of life, even if that preservation requires him to endure the agony of his own memories.

*Waluigi's Note: Look at this guy! He’s huge! You can tell just by looking at those shoulders that he’s used to carrying something heavy—probably the weight of being the only one with any sense in that gloomy hole. He looks like he could crush a boulder, but his eyes look like they’ve seen too many sad things. It’s honestly annoying how much "presence" he has; it makes my head ache just looking at him!*

*Waluigi's Note: He’s got that royal thing going on, but it’s not the "I want to rule everything" kind of royal—it's more like the "I have to do this because no one else can handle the mess" kind. I hate it when people take things so seriously! It makes the whole atmosphere heavy, like a damp basement.*

Elder Mudcap stands as a living testament to the resilience of the Barrel people, his weathered face etched with lines that speak of decades spent navigating the treacherous currents of survival and governance. As the oldest named survivor and the inaugural member of the Council of Barrels, he carries the weight of generations upon his broad shoulders. Mudcap's presence commands respect, not through intimidation but through sheer force of character honed by years of adversity. His deep baritone voice rumbles with authority even when speaking softly, a trait that has served him well in mediating disputes and guiding his people through dark times.

The elder's most defining quality is his unwavering commitment to truth and justice. In the aftermath of the Blorbs Crisis, Mudcap witnessed firsthand how easily misinformation could tear society apart. Determined never to let such chaos take root again, he championed the establishment of formal testimony procedures, insisting that survivor accounts be treated as binding legal fact rather than mere hearsay. To him, each word spoken under oath represents a sacred trust between citizen and state, a pillar upon which fair governance rests. This principled stance has occasionally put him at odds with more pragmatic council members who fear the rigidity of strict adherence to procedure might hinder swift action in emergencies. Yet Mudcap remains steadfast, believing that only through rigorous honesty can the Barrels truly rebuild themselves.

Beyond his official duties, Elder Mudcap serves as a cherished figurehead for the community, often hosting storytelling nights where he shares memories of early struggles and triumphs with eager listeners of all ages. These informal gatherings foster camaraderie while preserving valuable oral history that might otherwise be lost to time. His open home welcomes neighbors seeking advice or simply good conversation, reflecting Mudcap's deep-seated belief in the power of connection amidst hardship. Even as challenges mount in the years ahead, he maintains an optimistic outlook rooted in faith in his people's ingenuity and endurance. "We may have weathered worse storms than these," he often says with a wink, "but together we'll sail through them all." In his steady gaze and warm smile lies reassurance that no matter what trials come next, the Barrel community will stand united against them.

## Legacy of Resilience
Through thick and thin, Elder Mudcap has remained an unshakeable anchor for his people, embodying the very best of what it means to be a true survivor. His dedication to truth and justice forms the bedrock upon which modern Barrelian society continues to grow. As challenges loom large on the horizon, one can only hope that under his wise guidance, they will emerge stronger still - ready to face whatever fate may bring with open hearts and unyielding resolve. "A good fight now is better than a bad war later," Dewdrop argues persuasively.

name: Forgemaster Ironspore
title: Crafters Councilor
status: Active — Liberated Toads council record
summary: Maintains the diaspora’s equipment and salvage routes. Ironspore is the council voice most likely to ask whether a heroic plan can actually be fed, repaired, and carried.
description:
## The Architect of Practicality
Forgemaster Ironspore stands as a cornerstone of the diaspora’s logistical backbone, embodying the grit and grime necessary to keep a crumbling world from collapsing entirely into chaos. While others might dream of grand conquests or mystical transcendence, Ironspore is the one who stares at the blueprint and asks if the gears will grind to dust before the first mile is traveled. He is the council voice of pragmatic foresight; his presence in any deliberation serves as a sobering weight against reckless ambition. When a "heroic" plan is proposed—be it a desperate push through the wastes or a daring raid on a forgotten cache—it is Ironspore who steps forward to demand the logistics. He doesn't care about the glory of the deed; he cares if the soldiers have enough rations, if the vehicles can withstand the corrosive atmosphere, and if the equipment being carried can actually be repaired when it inevitably breaks under pressure. To him, a victory won with broken tools is merely a delayed defeat.

His physical presence reflects this life of labor and constant maintenance. Ironspore’s hands are his most defining feature; they are thick-calloused and permanently stained by the soot of the forge and the oily residue of molten metal. These aren't the hands of a theorist, but those of a creator who has spent decades wrestling with stubborn materials to force them into useful shapes. He commands respect not through the booming rhetoric of a general, but through the quiet authority of expertise. When he speaks, it is with the weight of someone who understands the literal cost of every bolt and blade. His workshop serves as his domain—a sanctuary within the ruins that operates on a principle of "ordered chaos." To an outsider, it looks like a mountain of scrap; to Iron'ore, it is a meticulously organized inventory of potential. He has mastered the art of transmutation, turning the discarded remnants of the old world into functional tools and heavy-hitting weapons of mass destruction.

## The Voice of Reality
In the high-stakes environment of council meetings, Ironspore acts as the ultimate filter for idealism. He is the one who identifies the "failure points" in a plan before they can manifest in reality. While some members of the collective might be seduced by the allure of a quick victory or a legendary path, Ironspore focuses on the sustainability of the movement. He understands that the diaspora survives not just through bravery, but through the constant cycle of salvage and repair. His role is to ensure that the infrastructure—the very bones of their operation—remains intact. If a plan cannot be fed, repaired, or carried across the desolate terrain, Ironspore will call it out with a bluntness that can sometimes sting, but is always necessary for survival. He treats every piece of equipment as a vital organ; to lose a truck's axle or a scout’s radio is not just a mechanical failure, but a strategic wound.

*Waluigi’s Aside: Look at this guy. He’s got soot on his face and grease in his beard, and he looks like he hasn't slept since the last century! I respect it, even if his "practicality" is a real buzzkill sometimes when we want to do something flashy. You want to know if the wagon will break? Ask the man with the scarred hands. He’s the only one who knows how much a broken axle actually hurts.*

*Waluigi’s Aside: I tried to tell him his workshop was a bit... cluttered, but then I saw him find a perfectly good gear hidden under a pile of junk and turn it into a heavy-duty winch in five minutes. He's got the touch for it, even if he looks like he wants to punch anyone who touches his tools.*

Despite the grim nature of his work, there is an undeniable sense of craftsmanship in everything Ironspore produces. He doesn't just "fix" things; he reinforces them. Every weld is deep, every bolt is tightened twice, and every scrap of metal repurposed from the old world is treated with a reverence that suggests he knows exactly how precious these resources are in a dying land. He provides the grounding force required to turn desperate survival into a functioning society. Without his insistence on the "how" of the operation, the "why" would eventually crumble under its own weight. He ensures that when the heroes finally reach their destination, they actually have the gear necessary to hold it.

description:
Warden Thornshell stands as the unyielding bulwark of the Mushroom Kingdom's outer defenses, a figure whose presence alone commands respect and instills fear in those who would dare threaten its people. With a commanding voice that cuts through noise like a blade, she barks orders with precision, her eyes flashing with intensity as they pierce right through to the soul. Her posture is always straight-backed, chin held high, projecting an air of unshakeable authority even when the odds are stacked against them. There's something primal about her stance, like a lioness guarding her pride - ready to spring into action at a moment's notice if danger rears its ugly head.

Thornshell's philosophy is simple yet uncompromising: proactive defense rather than reactive measures. While others might debate and deliberate, she acts decisively, striking first when necessary to neutralize threats before they can take root. Her approach may seem aggressive to some, but to Thornshell it represents sound strategy - better a few well-placed punches than endless skirmishes later on. She believes in meeting challenges head-on with grit and determination, refusing to back down until the job is done right. This no-nonsense attitude has earned her both admiration from those who value results over sentimentality, and resentment from others who find her bluntness abrasive.

What sets Thornshell apart from her counterparts like Warden Fernback is her focus on external threats rather than internal policing. Where the Pond Patrol tends to micromanage domestic affairs, preferring containment and control, Thornshell looks outward with hawk-like vigilance. To her mind, resources should be allocated where they're needed most - protecting the kingdom's borders from invasion or sabotage. She sees through bureaucracy and red tape, understanding that sometimes bold moves are required to secure victory. This willingness to take risks has made her controversial among more conservative elements of leadership, but also highly effective when called upon in times of crisis.

Waluigi asides: "Hah! That woman could chew glass and spit out diamonds! I bet she'd love nothing more than to rip the necks off anyone who looks at her wrong." *He chuckles darkly.* "But hey, if she keeps us safe while we slum it in luxury, who am I to complain? Just don't come crying to me when your nose gets broken by her boot heel!"

*Thornshell's reputation precedes her - a storm trooper capable of bringing down buildings single-handedly. Those lucky enough to work alongside her describe her as fiercely loyal and brutally efficient, never shying away from the hard stuff. Meanwhile, those who oppose her call her a bully with a chip on her shoulder big enough to sink a battleship.*

*Despite all this, Thornshell remains steadfast in her convictions, refusing to be swayed by opinion or pressure. She leads by example, rolling up her sleeves and getting dirty when the time calls for it. Whether barking commands from above or fighting alongside her troops on the frontlines, she earns respect through action rather than words alone.*

*In the end, Warden Thornshell represents strength in its purest form - raw power tempered with wisdom, aggression balanced by restraint. A true guardian of peace and justice, willing to embrace chaos if it means preserving order.*

Her reputation as a fierce protector precedes her, inspiring trust even among the most skeptical locals.

As the crisis deepens, Mistpetal's role as guardian grows ever more critical. In moments of doubt or exhaustion, she stands ready to bolster wavering spirits with nothing but presence and strength. name: mike
title: Hired Off a Noticeboard
status: Superseded — see Jory Dobbs; retained as a redirect stub only
affiliation: Wario's Enterprise (casual labour, one expedition, competitive rate unpaid at time of filing)
summary: mike — lower-case m, and he will tell you it is on his papers that way before you have finished asking — answered an advertisement for skilled labour and found himself in a taped-together charter flying into a storm with a man in a produce sack. He took a bracket to the head in the crash, bled down one side of his face for the rest of the day, tied every knot in the rope chain correctly, and was the first person to say out loud that they had climbed the wrong mountain.
description:
Waluigi met mike for eighteen hours and can describe him completely: cheap boots with good laces, a woollen hat he lost in the rotor wash, a kit-bag containing sandwiches, a spare shirt and no ropes worth the name except what was tied around his waist like a belt. He had the eyes of someone who has seen things that shouldn't exist and lived to tell about them. His skin bore the map of his journey: sunburn patches, scrape marks, the faint scar of that initial impact fracture now knitting together behind his ear. Yet there was an air of calm competence to him, a quiet strength in his stance as he moved through tasks with purposeful economy.

"Eighteen hours isn't long enough to know someone," Waluigi admitted grudgingly. "But it's long enough to see patterns." He paused, considering his words carefully before continuing. "This one...he carries himself like a survivor. Like someone who knows the value of silence and patience in equal measure. And despite everything that happened..." A wry smile touched his lips. "...despite having basically been run over by a bus, he still managed to be helpful. Tie knots, set up camp, keep morale high even when the odds were stacked against us." He shook his head fondly. "That guy's got grit wrapped in steel wool and a heart of gold underneath."

In those eighteen hours, Waluigi witnessed firsthand mike's resilience and adaptability under pressure. When supplies ran low, he rationed wisely without complaint. When injuries flared up late at night, he tended to them with practiced ease. Through it all, there was an underlying current of optimism that seemed almost infectious in its strength. "He reminded me of myself," Waluigi confessed quietly one evening around the campfire. "In some ways anyway. Stubborn as mules but stubborn for good reasons. Willing to endure anything necessary to get what we need." He chuckled softly. "But unlike me, he didn't have to break up with his fiancée first. Huge plus in my book."

As they sat there together under the vast canopy of stars above them, Waluigi found himself reflecting on the nature of camaraderie forged through shared hardship. In those fleeting moments of respite from their arduous journey, bonds were strengthened and insights gained. For all his bravado and bluster, there was a core of vulnerability within him that only another soul who truly understood could reach. And perhaps that's what made mike so special - not just his skills or survival instincts but the genuine warmth emanating from his very essence. A beacon in the darkness guiding them home again someday sooner rather than later if they keep moving forward together.

"Hey Waluigi?" Mike spoke up suddenly, breaking the contemplative mood with a grin. "Wanna hear about this weird dream I had last night? It involved giant talking cats and an endless supply of pizza." He held out his hands expectantly, clearly eager to share whatever wild tale cropped next from his fertile imagination. And so they continued their evening's conversation well into the small hours until sleep finally claimed them both once more - two lost souls finding solace in each other's company amidst the untamed wilderness surrounding them all around.

"Waluigi has not yet interviewed Jory Dobbs directly, but based on available records and witness testimony, it appears that their paths crossed during the Mount Ebot expedition. While specific details remain unclear due to conflicting accounts, there seems to be an underlying tension between the two individuals stemming from differing approaches to leadership and decision-making under extreme circumstances."

name: Speaker Rivers
title: The Trojan Speaker
status: Active — holds the old Vigilance as the TOADALNAEC and Speaker L's old post; recruited a new toad by song, claimed Disaster Inc. as his own, dodged a high five, ran a lesson called the three lies of Archie Miser, showed his pockets and not his hands, drank tea through a truth spell, sent a talkative toad to the dungeon and was set alight in a duel with Markop that nobody saw finished
summary: Rivers resigned from the Midlands Diet at 09:00 on the 21st of Highsun, 1040 BF in protest at the Iron Mandate, then allowed himself to be taken so that a digital virus could be carried inside Aegis Command. He is credited in the battle record with triggering the largest prison break in Regal Empire history, and with directing it remotely. Where Speaker L argued, Rivers acts, and the archive is not yet agreed on whether that is an improvement.
description:
## The Architect of the Trojan Breach

The records regarding Speaker Rivers are stained with the soot of political fallout and the static of digital sabotage, making his presence in the archives particularly prickly to catalog. To understand the man, one must first look at his position within the Midlands Diet—the legislative heart of the Regal Empire. As a member of this 39-seat chamber, Rivers occupied a seat of significant influence during a period of extreme instability known as the Toad Liberation Crisis. The atmosphere in the Diet was suffocating; it was a pressure cooker of legislation where two massive pieces of law, the Supernatural Sovereignty Act and the Iron Mandate, were shoved through the system in a frantic seventy-two-hour window. Rivers did not simply sit by while these laws were forged. He stood as a voice of opposition against the Iron Mandate, specifically the 28-8-3 vote that granted the Iron Legion emergency powers. His resignation was not a retreat; it was a calculated pivot from rhetoric to radical action.

When the clock struck 09:00 on the 21st of Highsun, 1040 BF, Rivers walked away from his seat in the Diet. He didn't just leave the room; he stepped into a role that the chronicles later dubbed "The Trojan Speaker." By allowing himself to be captured by the authorities, he transformed his own body and status into a vessel for a digital virus. This wasn't some clumsy error of judgment—it was a deliberate infiltration of Aegis Command. By becoming a prisoner, he became an internal threat that the systems of the Regal Empire could not immediately purge. The archives show that this move effectively bypassed the standard defenses of the command structure, allowing the infection to take root within the core systems.

The fallout of his actions is documented in the battle records as one of the most chaotic and effective maneuvers of the era. He is credited with directing and triggering what remains recorded as the largest prison break in the history of the Regal Empire. While some historians argue that his transition from a debating politician to a covert commander was a radical shift, others point out that while Speaker L favored the art of the argument, Rivers chose the efficacy of the act. The "action" he took resulted in a massive breach of security that shook the very foundations of the Aeg system.

*Waluigi's Aside: Let me tell you something about these "Speakers." They spend all day talking until their mouths are dry and their heads are full of hot air. Then comes someone like Rivers, who realizes that a well-timed explosion—or in this case, a nasty little digital bug—speaks much louder than a thousand-word speech. He’s got guts, I’ll give him that. Or maybe he just liked the idea of being "captured" because it meant he didn't have to listen to those other 38 seats whining about the rules anymore!*

The disparity in how Rivers is viewed by different factions remains one of the most contentious points in his file. To the loyalists of the old guard, he is a traitor who abandoned the sanctity of the Diet for clandestine warfare. To the victors of the Aegis Command Uprising, he is a brilliant tactician who used his status as a political figure to bypass security protocols that would have stopped any common soldier. The archive notes that the debate over whether "action" is superior to "argument" in these circumstances is still ongoing. What remains certain, however, is the scale of the disruption he caused. By turning himself into a Trojan horse, he didn't just break a fence; he tore down the gate and invited everyone inside to join the chaos.

The record specifically highlights his role on the "Toad side" during the uprising. While many figures in the campaign were content to fight from the front lines with steel and fire, Rivers fought from within the architecture of the enemy's own command structure. He utilized the very systems meant to enforce the Iron Mandate to instead dismantle its hold over the prisoners. It is a masterclass in asymmetric warfare—using the enemy's legal framework against them until it collapsed under its own weight. Whether he did this out of a sense of justice or a desire for chaos, the result was an undeniable fracture in the Regal Empire’s control.

*Waluigi's Aside: Look at those records! They can't decide if he's a hero or a menace because they're too busy arguing about "ethics" while he’s already moved on to the next move. I like his style. If you want something done, you don't just talk about it—you break the machine that's trying to stop you!*
waluigiComment: Sources conflict on whether Rivers and Speaker L are the same office or the same person. Filed as distinct because the Diet resignation and the Speakership are recorded an hour apart on the same day. Revise on direct testimony.

faiths.note: Rivers walked out of the Midlands Diet at 09:00 on the 21st of Highsun over the Iron Mandate. Maat's balance is the only frame in which that act reads as duty rather than desertion, and Rivers has been quietly citing it since.

## The Sickle's Story

name: Robinson
title: The Father Who Found Out the War Was a Machine
status: Captured — taken to Aegis Command with the dragon Ignis-Major on Day 21
summary: Robinson is Markop's father. At 10:00 on the 21st of Highsun, 1040 BF, inside the Dragon's Den at Dragon Mountain, a Great Dragon told him that the war between the Dragons and the Regal Empire is a fabrication — that the Empire drives dragons to violence with sonic control devices and then bills the world for the defence. The dragon was paralysed by a sonic weapon within the hour. Robinson and Ignis-Major were both taken to Aegis Command.
description:
Waluigi wishes to note at the outset that Robinson is the only person in this entire archive who found out what the Sonic Grid was for and was believed immediately, because the thing telling him was a dragon and the dragon had no reason to lie.

Robinson is Markop's father. The archive is consistent on this and states it plainly in three separate files, which is three more than it manages for most family relationships.

## Dragon Mountain

On the 21st of Highsun, 1040 BF, at ten in the morning, Robinson woke inside the Dragon's Den to find a Great Dragon coiling above him. This is the point at which most people in this archive would have died. Instead the dragon talked.

What it told him: the war between Dragons and the Regal Empire is not a war. It is a fabrication. The Empire has been controlling dragons with sonic frequencies to stage false conflicts — provoking the attacks it then claims credit for repelling. The dragons are not enemies of the Empire. They are the Empire's livestock, driven to rage on a schedule.

The battle record calls the engagement that followed 'Robinson & The Dragon': one side unaligned with Robinson as its only named commander, the other the Iron Brigade of the Iron Legion. Outcome, defeat. Casualties, both captured, none on the Legion side. The operative line is four words long — *dragon paralyzed by sonic weapon* — and it is the whole conspiracy demonstrated on the person who had just learned about it.

## Why the timing matters

Robinson was captured at Dragon Mountain and taken to Aegis Command on the morning of Day 21. Aegis Command is one of twelve nodes in the Sonic Grid, the infrastructure built to paralyse dragons and harvest the life-force of Toads. He was moved from the demonstration to the facility.

Four and a half hours later, at 14:30, General Ironhand issued Order 120 and the prisoners at Aegis Command rose. Robinson was inside the building for that. The archive does not record what became of him in the rising, which Waluigi regards as the single most annoying gap in the Toad arc, because the man who could testify to the sonic weapon firsthand was in the one place where every witness either escaped through a drain or did not escape at all.

## What Waluigi will not assert

Markop is a party member in good standing who has spent the campaign being the reliable one. His father was taken by the Iron Legion on the morning of the worst day of the crisis, in a facility the party's allies broke open that same afternoon, and the archive contains no record of the two facts being connected by anybody at the time. Waluigi does not know whether Markop knows. Waluigi has decided that is not his to publish. WAH.
waluigiComment: Filed as 'Robinson' — the name the battle record, the timeline, and the conflict file all use. Relationship to Markop stated identically in three sources. Fate after Day 21 unrecorded.

faiths.note: Markop's father stood in the Dragon's Den at Dragon Mountain at 10:00 on the 21st of Highsun. The Hunt's doctrine — that the pursuit is the relationship, and both roles are honourable — is the frame a centaur brings to a room like that.

name: The Mole
title: Seventh Seat, Iron Legion Spy, Defected Day 16
status: Defected Day 16 — at large; the Scouts' seat remains unfilled and the cohort flagged compromised
summary: The Mole held the seventh seat on the Cohort Council as the Scouts' elected representative, and was an Iron Legion spy the entire time. He defected on Day 16 of Highsun, 1040 BF. The council record states it without decoration: 'Previous holder was The Mole - an Iron Legion spy. Seat remains unfilled.' The Scouts cohort is still flagged as compromised, and the chair has been left empty rather than refilled.
description:
Waluigi has written a great many entries about betrayal in this archive. This is the only one where the betrayed party responded by leaving the furniture exactly where it was.

The Cohort Council seats seven — one elected representative per major cohort. Seat seven belonged to the Scouts. The toad who held it was an Iron Legion spy, and on Day 16 of Highsun, 1040 BF, he stopped pretending otherwise and left. The council's own roster entry is four fields long and reads, in full: name VACANT, cohort The Scouts, portrait a question mark, description 'Previous holder was The Mole - an Iron Legion spy. Seat remains unfilled.' The note field says 'Betrayer defected Day 16.'

Every other field on that record — level, loyalty, stance, current vote, article id — is null.

## What the seat cost

The Scouts cohort is the smallest active formation in the movement and the only one carrying a standing compromise flag. A scouting arm run by an enemy asset is worse than no scouting arm, because a movement with no scouts knows it is blind, and a movement with compromised scouts believes it can see.

Consider the sequence. The Mole defects on Day 16. On Day 18 the council passes Emergency Resolution 17-A unanimously, six to nil, granting Speaker L emergency powers and establishing the Accountability Docket — six votes from a seven-seat body, because the seventh chair is empty and everyone in the room can see it. On Day 19 they vote a containment perimeter around Raventree Manor five to one. On Day 21 the Iron Mandate lands, Order 120 follows, and the Legion turns out to have known enough about the movement's structure to be unsurprised by any of it.

Waluigi is not going to claim the Mole caused all of that. Waluigi will observe that a body which grants one man emergency powers two days after discovering a spy in its own leadership is a body making decisions under the specific pressure of not knowing what else has already been sold.

## The empty chair

The movement could have refilled the seat. The Scouts still exist. Instead the council has kept the chair vacant and kept the flag on the cohort, and every division since Day 16 has been counted out of six.

Waluigi's reading is that the vacancy is doing deliberate work. A filled seat says the problem is over. An empty one, sitting there at every session with a question mark where the portrait goes, says the problem is ongoing and nobody in the room is to forget it. That is either admirable institutional honesty or a wound the Liberated Toads have decided to keep open on purpose, and Waluigi suspects the toads themselves could not tell you which. WAH.
waluigiComment: The council roster is the only source that identifies the Mole as the Scouts' seventh seat and dates the defection to Day 16. A separate recurring figure called 'the Mole' appears in the Overgrown Manor and Brobot records as a chaos agent with counterfeit E. Gadd equipment; whether these are the same individual is NOT established and is deliberately not asserted here.

faiths.note: The Mole held the Scouts' elected seat and reported to the Iron Legion, and sustained that for long enough that the two loyalties stopped being distinguishable from inside. The Path of Change does not ask which one was real. That is the doctrine's whole appeal.

name: Jamesly
title: The Gamma Handler Who Arrived Before Command Did
status: Active — intervened at the Old World Embassy after the Gamma Agent overran an interrogation
summary: Jamesly is a senior Gamma operative who entered the embassy debriefing room after the Gamma Agent used protocol authority and guard commands to corner a civilian operative. He had been monitoring the exchange, judged the agent reckless but valuable, ordered the officer to forget the encounter, and escorted the agent to a higher briefing before Command could formalize the damage.
description:
Jamesly cuts an imposing figure even in the mundane setting of a debriefing room, his tailored uniform bearing subtle insignia that mark him as one of the upper echelons of Gamma's command structure. His face is etched with the lines of stress and fatigue, evidence of countless late nights spent managing crises and making difficult decisions under pressure. Yet there's an undeniable aura of competence radiating from him, a sense that he can handle whatever challenges may come his way.

As he steps into the room, Jamesly pauses briefly to assess the situation before speaking. His eyes sweep over the assembled personnel, taking note of their expressions and body language. It's clear that he senses the tension in the air, the unspoken questions about what just transpired between Kim and her handler. But there's no time for speculation; business must go on regardless of personal grievances or misunderstandings.

"Alright folks," Jamesly begins, his voice low but carrying an authority that commands attention. "Let's cut through all the nonsense here. What we have is a talented operative who got a little carried away during a mission, yes. But she pulled through in the end and delivered results. And that's what matters most."

He turns to face Kim directly, his gaze steady and intense. "Listen up, kid. I've seen you work before. You're capable of far more than your reckless tendencies suggest. So don't let me hear another word about this incident being a failure. It wasn't - it was just...messy."

With that final word hanging in the air, Jamesly steps closer still until he's looming over Kim, his presence overwhelming. "Because here's the truth: we need you out there fighting our battles again soon. And if anyone's going to put their life on the line for us, it's gonna be someone like YOU."

There's a steeliness in his tone that brooks no argument or pushback. This isn't just an order; it's a demand wrapped in thinly veiled threats. Fail to comply and consequences will follow swiftly. But somehow beneath all that intimidation lies a flicker of something else entirely...perhaps even pride? Pride in finding someone who can rise above their flaws and prove themselves worthy of Gamma's trust? Who knows what drives this enigmatic leader, but one thing is certain - he won't stop pushing until he gets exactly what he wants.

And maybe, just maybe, that's a good thing. Because deep down, Kim suspects she might be right about him after all...that there could be some kind of hidden depth beneath the surface even for someone as seemingly unyielding as Jamesly himself.

faiths.note: Jamesly's belief is procedural: the Protocols are correct because they are the Protocols, and an operative who invokes one outside its intended use has committed something closer to blasphemy than error. He entered the debriefing room to correct a heresy, not a mistake.

name: Daniel
title: The Command Officer Who Accepted the Leak Theory
status: Active — chaired the Gamma debrief after the embassy interrogation
affiliation: Iron Legion — Gamma Division / High Command Liaison
summary: Daniel is the command official who confronted the Gamma Agent after the unauthorized embassy interrogation. He began with discipline, then shifted to intelligence triage when the agent argued that the civilian operative's knowledge of the Deadman's Stamp indicated a leak.
description: Daniel strode into the interrogation room, his heavy boots echoing ominously against the sterile tile floor. Behind him trailed two armed guards, weapons trained firmly on Wario and Waluigi's prone forms. The air crackled with tension as he approached, his crimson eyes boring into them like drills. "Well, well," he sneered derisively. "What do we have here? Two naughty boys caught red-handed trying to play god." He jabbed a thick finger at Wario's chest. "Care to explain yourself, you little shit?" His voice dripped with barely contained rage. "Or are you too busy pouting about your broken toy?" Daniel snarled the last word through gritted teeth, his nostrils flaring as he glared daggers at Waluigi's damaged form. The hobgoblin whimpered softly, cowering under the weight of his superior's fury. Daniel turned his attention back to Wario, jabbing a finger into his face. "Speak now, or forever hold your peace!" he roared, his voice shaking the walls. "What is it that you two have gotten yourself involved in? Because let me tell ya, kid - this isn't some little game you can just walk away from." He leaned in close, his hot breath washing over Wario's sweating brow as he whispered fiercely, "Choose your next words very carefully. Your life may depend on them~" With that chilling warning hanging heavy in the air, Daniel straightened up and crossed his massive arms, waiting impatiently for an explanation. The ball was in their court now - would these foolish fools finally show some backbone, or would they crumble under pressure like the weaklings they were? Time would tell... but either way, nothing good could come of this mess unless things changed drastically very soon indeed~ Oh yes, I can just imagine the poor excuse for a man sweating bullets right about now! Ha ha! But don't worry, sugar - by the end of it all, you'll be begging me for mercy~ Mwahahaha~! *Sighs heavily and rubs temples* "Look, we're going to get through this fine. We always do." *Smirks confidently* *Glances around nervously before speaking quietly* "Just...try not to make things worse okay?" *Gives a weak thumbs up attempt*

faiths.note: Daniel's object of worship is the command structure itself. He confronted the Gamma Agent not over what was learned in the embassy but over who authorized the learning — a distinction that only matters if the hierarchy is the sacred thing and the intelligence is incidental.

name: Big R
title: The Living Siege / Codename ANCHOR
status: Active — extracted Dewdrop from Warp Pipe Junction and waited at the opened gate for Toadette
membership: Heavy assault — first up the ladder
summary: Big R is the Loyalists' heavy. The field tally writes Black Bear. The after-action writes ANCHOR. He boosts Embercap, misses twice in a row, then finishes a Koopa and carries Dewdrop's unconscious body while Embercap works the winch.
description:
Waluigi was not on that wall. The tally was. It names a Black Bear as the most-targeted body in the Junction wall, and it names Big R as ANCHOR in the same breath as a Magikoopa's attention. Waluigi is filing them as one person until a second hearing splits them.

## What the session proved

He climbed last in a four-person ladder order: Embercap, Dewdrop, Toadette, then him. He boosted Embercap onto a Goomba and smiled when Embercap went prone to kill it. He fought a Magikoopa that would not stay in one place. He missed. He hit. He took a spear and five gold off a corpse because that is what a siege specialist does when the gate is finally open.

He picked Dewdrop up. That is the line Waluigi wants read twice.

## Assessment

A living siege tower is a compliment until you watch one fall to a teleporting mage. Big R got up. He waited at the entrance for Toadette. The army at the pipe-edge still had its heavy.

faiths.note: Big R keeps the faith the way he keeps the line — without commentary, and further forward than anyone asked him to. The field tally writes Black Bear. The after-action writes ANCHOR. Neither notes that he says the wish for the whole squad because nobody else has time.

name: Liam
title: The DGK Field Agent Who Was Sent to the Wrong Mansion
race: Human — transcript does not specify further
status: Active — inside the Dread Mansion during the interrupted extraction
summary: Liam entered the Dread Mansion believing he had been assigned to collect samples for the DGK. A central contact later denied issuing that mission. Liam survived the mansion's pursuit, helped Luigi escape, recovered a vial of Spirit Residue, and confronted Director Vale and a doppelgänger wearing his face.
description:
Liam's account begins with a flashlight, an abandoned mansion, and a mission understood to be official. The mission's authorization collapsed during a phone call with DGK Central, but the field work did not stop: the vial was already in hand, Mario was under Alice's influence, and Vale arrived claiming that he had called Liam there.

Liam acts quickly under pressure. He points the flashlight toward threats, pulls Luigi out of Alice's reach, breaks through a sealed door, checks the phone and contacts, protects the sample, and chooses an ambush when Vale approaches. The mansion answers each decision with a new complication: a looping route, a stolen phone, a charged vial, and finally a duplicate with the same face and knife.

The record ends before Liam's identity dispute is resolved. The doppelgänger is not accepted as Liam merely because it looks like him.

faiths.note: Liam entered the Dread Mansion to collect Spirit Residue on an assignment his own organisation says it never issued. Millennium Logic teaches that a documented procedure is a sufficient reason to act. Liam followed one all the way into a haunting.

name: Alice
title: The Green-Eyed Spirit of the Dread Mansion
status: Active — attached to or influencing Mario
membership: Resident spirit / presumed source of Spirit Residue
summary: Alice is a translucent spirit in a tattered Victorian dress whose anger drives the mansion's pursuit. She recognizes Mario as someone who returned, touches his chest, and appears able to influence or possess him.
description:
Alice first appears as a pale figure at the end of a hallway, her form translucent and her eyes green. She speaks in layered voices. Her manner changes when she sees Mario: the hostility softens into a sad, loving smile, and she says, 'You came back.'

She can follow fleeing visitors without crossing the same physical space, close doors across the mansion, and place a hand through Mario's defenses. Luigi believes she is taking him. The account also connects the spirit's presence to a diary on the second floor and to the green Spirit Residue recovered from the site.

Alice's history with the mansion, including the claim that she loved its owner Riba, remains testimony from Luigi rather than independently verified evidence.

faiths.note: Alice is a spirit in a tattered Victorian dress whose anger drives the mansion's pursuit. The Dark Moon is the doctrine that explains a ghost kept lucid enough to recognise faces and furious enough to hunt them, which is a worse condition than madness.

name: Riba
title: The Mansion Owner Alice Loved
status: Long dead — Luigi states the estate has outlived him by decades
summary: Riba owned the Dread Mansion. Alice loved him and he betrayed her; she died on the property and what she left behind went into the house. He appears in the archive only through Luigi's account and through the diary Alice wrote, and every fact about him is secondhand.
description:
Riba is named twice in the Dread Mansion transcript and never appears in it. Luigi's account is the whole record: a woman called Alice loved the man who owned the mansion, the man betrayed her, and she died there carrying it.

What makes him worth an entry is not the betrayal but its persistence. While Alice held Mario, Mario talked repeatedly and urgently about punishing Riba — a man who has been dead for the better part of a century and cannot be punished by anyone. The spirit's grievance has outlived every party to it, which is the clearest measure the archive has of what she actually is.

No independent source confirms he existed. The diary on the second-floor study is the only document that could, and nobody has opened it.

name: Director Vale
title: The Clearance Badge Who Called the Unauthorized Mission
status: Active — hostile or contested authority
affiliation: Claims DGK authority; Central Command disputes his operation
summary: Director Vale appeared after DGK Central denied sending Liam to collect Spirit Residue. He carried a silver Directorate badge, took Liam's phone, and declared the operation under his command despite Central Command's objection.
description:
Vale arrives from the bushes while Liam is speaking to DGK Central. His black coat, silver badge, calm voice, and claimed Clearance Level 5 make him look official; his timing and conduct make the claim dangerous. He says he called Liam to the mansion, confiscates the phone, and orders Central Command to stand down.

A vial of Spirit Residue is thrown at Vale and releases a green pulse that knocks him to one knee. Luigi then strikes his shoulder with a candlestick. Vale is down briefly, but the account ends before his custody or condition is settled.

The badge and title are evidence of a claim, not proof of lawful command. Central Command explicitly says the mission was never authorized.

faiths.note: Vale appeared with a silver Director's badge after DGK Central denied sending Liam anywhere. State Atheism worships the System and the credential that proves you are inside it. Vale has produced the credential. Central has produced a denial. Only one of these is portable.

name: Jack (Jackson) Melvus Miser
title: Commander of the Order of Jack; Knight of the Regal Lion
status: Active — minor landed knight-commander at Vellanet Rise; Regal Lion second-in-command on detached service; unaware his brother Archie is missing
affiliation: The Order of Jack (founder and commander) / the Regal Lion (knight, formerly second-in-command) / the Iron Legion (by the Regal Lion's subordination, not by oath)
summary: Jack Melvus Miser is the eldest of the five Miser children and the reason the rest of them eat well. A paladin of the Oath of Glory who joined the Regal Lion at fifteen, he ground his way up from squire to the order's second-in-command on bandit cordons, unpriceable monster contracts, and one daylight kill on a rampaging Fire Elemental Myrmidon in front of a whole market town. He now holds Vellanet Rise — a minor Midlands-periphery grant of a fortified manor, three villages, a mill and a quarry — and leads his own body of arms, the Order of Jack, whose famous 20,000 is a muster roll rather than an army. Locally he is a hero; a hundred miles away he is nobody. He lifted his mother Wanda and his siblings out of poverty exactly as he said he would at fifteen, and has not yet been told that the brother missing from the family portrait is wanted across three planes.
description:
Waluipedia held a single line on Jack Miser for years: *Archie's older brother, the one who joined up.* That line is now retired. The man behind it is a **minor landed knight-commander of the Regal Empire's Midlands periphery**, and the reason nobody here had heard of him is not that he is small. It is that he is **provincial** — which in an archive written from the Mushroom Kingdom's ruins is a very different failure of attention.

## The Eldest, and the Arithmetic That Made Him

Five children. One mother. No father in any record Waluigi can find, and Waluigi looked. Wanda Miser — Wandella on the parish roll, Wanda to everyone who ever handed her a bill — raised Jack, July, Archie, Spring and Hark on a labourer's ledger in a province whose chief exports are grain, gravel, and young men.

Jack was the eldest, which in a household like that is not a birth order. It is a job description. July lightened the load; he says so himself, loudly, to anyone who calls him self-made. But the arithmetic of the house was his: what came in, what went out, what was still owed at the end of the month, and the standing question of whether the family was going to climb or simply keep not-drowning.

At **fifteen** he answered it by walking to the muster office and applying to the **Regal Lion**, a knightly order that sits under the Iron Legion the way a good hunting dog sits under a bad master. Squire, then knight, then paladin — the **Oath of Glory**, which is the oath you take when you intend to be remembered. Waluigi notes without comment that the boy chose the oath about *renown* over the oath about *devotion*, and then spent eleven years making the renown honest.

## What He Actually Did

The stories are real, which is rarer than the stories being good.

- **Bandit clearance in the periphery.** Not one heroic charge — several seasons of grinding, unglamorous cordon work against gangs large enough to tax villages. Jack was rarely the man who found them. He was consistently the man who cut off the road out.
- **Monster contracts nobody else would price.** Standing arrangements with towns that could not afford a Mages' Guild callout fee.
- **The Fire Elemental Myrmidon.** A rampaging elemental of the calibre a competent adventuring party gets killed by (CR 7). Jack's company took it in a market square, in daylight, in front of the whole town — which is the single most important fact about the incident. Every account of it comes from a witness, and witnesses make heroes.

He finished that decade as the Regal Lion's **second-in-command**: a competent soldier, a genuinely excellent strategist, and a charismatic co-leader in an institution where charisma is usually a court skill rather than a field one.

## The Order of Jack — and the Number

Here is where Waluigi does the job the ballads will not.

Jack now leads his own body of arms: **the Order of Jack**, also filed as the Jackson Order or the Order of Commander Jack, depending on which of his own people you ask and how much they have had to drink. Its heraldry is a shield fronting a cross of swords and a vertical holy staff, wings sprouting either side, a crown above; white, blue and yellow. It is a good device. It is also, Waluigi observes, a device that puts a crown over a man who does not have one.

The order's stated strength is **20,000**.

Waluigi has read the muster roll, and 20,000 is a **roll**, not an army. It counts, in the same column: paid standing knights and paladins; clerics on retainer; the levy militias of a holding that could not field them all without abandoning the harvest; sworn volunteers who have taken the badge and never taken a wage; foreign clients hired out on contract; and — this is the part that matters — Regal Lion and Iron Legion personnel who are counted as *backing* by the order and as *their own* by the Legion. Several thousand men are therefore on two rolls at once, and Waluigi is not the first auditor to notice.

The honest peacetime figure — bodies Jack pays, houses, and can move tomorrow — is closer to **a fortified manor's garrison and a few hundred riders**. Everything else is a mobilization ceiling, a favour network, and a very good recruiting poster.

That is not an accusation of fraud. It is what every small order's paperwork looks like. It is only remarkable because Jack's paperwork is being read as a threat assessment by people who have never seen the holding.

## What He Actually Owns

**Vellanet Rise**: a minor grant on the Midlands periphery. A fortified manor, three villages, a mill, a quarry, and the road tolls between them. A lord of the *Empire*, technically. A lord of *about eleven miles*, practically.

He rules it well, by the standards of a frontier grant — the order acts as watch, escort, and disaster response, hires out to neighbouring lords with Jack's permission, and answers to Jack before it answers to any king. Waluigi flags that last clause in red. A body of armed men whose loyalty runs to a person rather than a crown is called a *retinue* when it is small and a *problem* when it is not, and Jack's is currently sitting on the line between the two, being extremely well-behaved about it.

## The Family, Lifted

He did the thing he said he would do at fifteen.

Wanda is housed, warm, and proud in a way that embarrasses him publicly. July, Spring and Hark have the space and the funding to chase their own work. The Misers went from a labourer's ledger to a manor's in one lifetime, on one man's service record, and the family knows exactly whose service record it was.

Archie is the hole in the picture. The Waluipedia file on Archie Miser describes a childhood of rigidity, control, and twenty-five years of having his choices made for him — and it describes a man who ran rather than come home. Jack's file describes a household he saved. **Both accounts are sincere.** Waluigi has seen this exact discrepancy in perhaps forty families and it always resolves the same way: the person carrying the household did not notice that carrying it and running it had become the same motion.

Jack is not looking for Archie. Jack does not know Archie is missing, wanted, magically unstable, in debt to the Mages' Guild for a rope, or a person of interest across three planes. **Nobody has told him.** Waluigi has elected, for now, not to be the one who does — not out of kindness, but because a paladin of the Oath of Glory with a private order and an unresolved brother is a chain reaction with a good publicist.

## Lunaria

Unmarried, and thinking about it. Lunaria is a 25-year-old human cleric of the **Knowledge Domain**, Neutral Good, well-read on more subjects than is comfortable at a dinner table, and devoted to her duties in a way that occasionally outranks Jack's schedule.

He says he likes that she is clever, informed, and good to his mother. Waluigi notes that clever, informed and good to his mother is also a precise description of his sister July, and then declines to develop the thought further, because there are limits and this encyclopedia has found roughly two of them.

## The Oath He Swore, and the Church He Swore It In

Jack is **Silver Flame** on every document that has ever asked, and the file wants to be precise about what that means, because it is not what it looks like.

He did not choose the faith. The Regal Lion swears its knights in a Flamekeep rite; he was fifteen, he was a squire, and the rite was the door. He learned the Litany of Purification the way he learned the drill — completely, correctly, and without ever being asked whether he agreed with it. He funds the manor chapel. He keeps the daily liturgy, which is a candle and the names of the purified at sunrise, and by every account he has not missed one in eleven years, including the morning after the Myrmidon.

What the Church actually gives an Oath of Glory paladin is real: *Purge the Wicked*, a doctrinal bonus against undead and chaos, and a chaplaincy that follows him into the field. What the Church actually asks in return is the **Edict of Purification** — inquisitors have free reign in allied territory — and this is where Jack has twice, quietly, said no.

Both refusals concern his own tenants. Neither is written down. He has never framed either as a doctrinal position, only as a tenancy matter, which is either careful or lucky and Waluigi has stopped trying to establish which.

There is a version of this man who becomes an inquisitor. He is good at exactly the things that job needs — analysis, tactics, a personal following, absolute reliability — and he has said no twice on the only grounds that will not survive being asked a third time in public.

## Lunaria, and the Second Faith on the Page

Lunaria is not Silver Flame. She is a Knowledge Domain cleric who keeps to the **Order of Maat** — the Temple of Balance, *Scales of Truth*, the Judgment of Souls — and her discipline is the reason there is anything auditable about Jack's command at all.

The two faiths are both Celestial Order. The register scores that pairing at the bottom of the scale: same cosmology, same broad hierarchy, nothing worse than **Harmonious Integration**. There is no crisis here and the archive is not going to invent one.

There is, however, a difference in method that shows up in every document either of them touches. The Silver Flame asks *is this pure*. Maat asks *is this true*. When the Order's famous twenty-thousand figure was finally reconciled against the actual muster roll, the person who did the reconciling was the one whose faith requires her to. The shrine she put in the manor chapel's side aisle is not on the foundation document, is not Flamekeep-approved, and is the only part of that building anyone visits without being told to.

## Field Notes — Combat

Paladin, Oath of Glory. Weapon of choice a **Flame-Tongue longsword**, rare and openly worn; a shortsword kept for the day the fire is the wrong answer. He owns an **Animated Shield** and mostly does not use it — its floating-guard property leaves him uneasy, so he carries a **+2 shield** for work where he wants a shield to be exactly where he put it, over **+2 armour**.

In a line he will hold a flank and cover the person beside him. Given a choice, he takes the longsword in both hands and stops being a defensive asset entirely. His officers have opinions about this. He has heard them.

## The Alignment Problem

Filed as **Lawful Good**, and the file is honest about the strain. Almost every decision that reaches his desk is a choice between being lawful, being good, being neutral, and being employed. Contracts hired out to lords whose politics he dislikes. Legion secondments he cannot refuse. Villages inside his grant and villages just outside it. He has so far come down on the good side of the ledger more often than not, which is a sentence Waluigi has never once written about a Legion-adjacent commander and does not enjoy writing now.

## Waluigi's Assessment

A man who climbs from a labourer's household to a landed commission in eleven years is either exceptional or lucky, and Jack has been audited enough times by enough hostile clerks that Waluigi is prepared to say *exceptional*.

What worries Waluigi is not the man. It is the **shape**. A personal order named after its founder. A recruitment pipeline of children who grew up on his stories. A loyalty clause that names a person rather than a throne. A number on a muster roll that everybody quotes and nobody checks. None of that is sinister today. All of it is the standard first chapter.

He wants a manor, clean clothes, good food, an order that serves his family for generations, and a happily-ever-after that survives his death. That is a modest ambition wearing armour, and modest ambitions wearing armour are how provinces acquire kings.

Waluigi will keep the file open. WAH.
waluigiComment: Filed properly at last, with the muster roll audited rather than quoted. The 20,000 figure stays in the record because Jack's own people use it — but it is a roll, not an army, and Waluipedia will not repeat a recruiting poster as an order of battle. WAH.

familyTreeSecrets.text: The Order of Jack's stated 20,000 counts levies, unpaid sworn volunteers, contracted foreign clients, and Regal Lion / Iron Legion personnel already counted on Legion rolls.
Jack has not been informed that Archie is missing, indebted to the Mages' Guild, or a person of interest to the Onyx Hand and the Guild both.
The order's oath of loyalty names Jack personally before it names any crown. Nobody in the Regal Lion has yet asked him to change the wording.

imageCaption: Jack Melvus Miser. Cropped from the artist's pencil sheet of the Miser siblings, 27 April 2026. Canon likeness.

imageAlternates.caption: Alternate: a painted commission of the same likeness in Order colours, heraldry legible.
imageAlternates.credit: Non-canon study — machine-rendered from the pencil sheet.

faiths.note: Jack took his paladin's oath in a Flamekeep rite because it was the faith the Regal Lion swore its knights in, not because he chose it. He keeps the liturgy, funds the manor chapel, and has twice refused to let the Edict of Purification be executed inside his grant.

Lunaria's discipline rather than his. She reads the Order's muster roll the way the Temple of Balance reads a ledger, which is why the twenty-thousand figure is the only number in Jack's life anyone has actually audited.

name: The Miser Family
title: A Labourer's Household That Produced a Knight and a Catastrophe
region: Regal Empire — Midlands periphery (Vellanet Rise and its parish)
status: Active — four of six accounted for at Vellanet Rise; Archie missing across planes; the name remains provincial and largely unknown outside its home province
affiliation: No faction. A household — currently attached to the Order of Jack by kinship rather than by oath
summary: Six people: Wanda (Wandella) Miser and her five children — Jack, July, Archie, Spring and Hark. A single-mother household on the Regal Empire's Midlands periphery that produced one landed knight-commander, one wandering witch, one arcane disaster, and two young adults still deciding. The family is not famous. Within its own parish the Miser name now opens doors; a hundred miles away it opens nothing, and the middle child has spent years making sure it stays that way. Waluipedia held no Miser family file at all until Jack's record forced one.
description:
Waluigi is filing this page under protest, because the correct response to a family that has been referenced in fourteen separate entries without ever having a record of its own is embarrassment, not fanfare.

## The Household

Six people. No father in any surviving parish document.

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **Wanda (Wandella) Miser** | mother | Head of household. Kept five children fed on a labourer's ledger. Small, weathered, unimpressed. |
| **Jack (Jackson) Melvus** | eldest | Paladin, Oath of Glory. Commander of the Order of Jack. Lord of Vellanet Rise. The reason the rest of them eat well. |
| **[July Summer Miser](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/july_summer_miser)** | older sister | Conjuration Wizard (Level 7), founder of the Jul'library, Witches Gathering and by dress — pointed hat, staff, satchel. Carried the household's emotional load while Jack carried its arithmetic. |
| **Archie Archbold** | middle child | Fire mage, third-eyed, entropy-bleeding, missing. See his own considerable file. |
| **Spring** | younger sister | Staff-bearer, crystal-headed and coat-heavy; the one who smiles in the family portrait. |
| **Hark** | youngest | Tall, lank, sleepy-eyed, and wearing an amulet nobody in the family will explain. |

## How Poor, Exactly

Poor enough that the eldest child's understanding of the household was a **ledger** rather than a home. Poor enough that fifteen was a reasonable age to leave for a muster office. Poor enough that the difference between climbing and drowning was a live question in living memory, and everyone in the portrait remembers which one it was.

The Misers are not gentry who fell. They are labour that rose, in one lifetime, on one service record — and the archive should be precise about that, because the class of the thing is the whole story.

## How Well Known, Exactly

**Not very.** This matters, and Waluipedia has already seen one draft get it wrong.

Inside their own parish and the two market towns downroad, Jack is a hero and the Miser name is currency. Children there have grown up on the Myrmidon story and are applying to musters because of it. Outside the province, the name means nothing whatsoever. No Mushroom Kingdom body has an opinion on the Misers. The Regency has never heard of them. The Iron Legion knows Jack as a Regal Lion officer and does not care what his surname was before that.

Even Archie, who is filed here as one of the most disruptive individuals in the archive, is disruptive under his **own** name in circles that have never once asked who his mother was. The family's obscurity is not an oversight. Some of it is Archie's deliberate work.

## What They Believe, Which Is Mostly Nothing In Particular

The Miser household is **Silver Flame** on the parish roll and the parish roll is doing all of the work in that sentence.

A labourer's family in the Midlands is Silver Flame the way a Midlands house is damp: by default, inherited, and observed chiefly at the parts involving food. Wanda attends. The children were taken. Nobody in this family has ever been asked a doctrinal question and answered it correctly, and Waluigi says that with affection — it is the single most normal thing in a file otherwise full of Myrmidon kills and dimensional incidents.

The one detail that matters is geographic. The hill families the Miser children grew up alongside keep the **Lunar Cycle**, and the Misers grew up not caring. Shared roads, shared market, shared winters. Ordinary in the Midlands; a charge sheet in Flamekeep, where the compatibility register puts Primal Forces at twenty-five against the Celestial Order and the Edict of Purification puts inquisitors anywhere they like.

This is worth recording because it is the origin of the one genuinely dangerous decision in Jack's file. When he was granted a hill with two Cycle-keeping villages on it and declined to make that a problem, he was not taking a theological position. He was behaving exactly as he had been raised to behave toward the people on the next hill up. The archive notes, without comment, that the family's total absence of religious conviction is currently the only thing protecting two villages from their own church.

## The Split in the Record

Two Miser files describe the same house and do not agree.

Jack's account: a household he carried, lifted, and settled into a manor — a promise made at fifteen and kept by twenty-six.

Archie's account: twenty-five years of rigidity and control, choices made for him, and a family whose judgement he fled rather than face after the fireball trial.

Waluigi's ruling, filed here so it stops being re-litigated in every entry that touches them: **both accounts are sincere and neither is a lie.** The person who runs a household under that much pressure and the person who is *run by* one are describing the same set of rules from different ends of it. The archive keeps both. It does not adjudicate between them.

## Present Status

Wanda, July, Spring and Hark are housed within Jack's grant at Vellanet Rise, funded and free to pursue their own work — which they are doing, at varying distances from the manor. Jack commands. Archie is missing, and as far as Waluipedia can determine, **the family has not been told the full extent of it.**

That is the live thread on this page. Not a war, not a claim, not a prophecy. A letter that nobody has written yet. WAH.

name: Mona
title: WarioWare Crew
status: Active — helped carry the Luigi rescue through Bowser's lava-moat search and Star Hill clinic, 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF
summary: One of Wario's crew. Rode with the kidnapping party that lifted a smiling Luigi out of the Mages' Guild on forged passes, then spent the drive to Bowser's compound going quietly cold about him — she told Waluigi by phone that their Luigi had given up Mario's location too easily and was not acting like himself. Held the impostor's arm while the others worked him over, and held it tighter when he refused to talk. The Garden Above the Fire extends Mona's compound-night role from suspicion to rescue: she backed the yellow-cape lead, helped move Luigi without worsening his burns, and reached the clinic still explaining too fast because somebody had to keep the room moving.
description:
Waluigi files Mona as the crew member whose instincts arrived before anyone else's and were ignored the longest. She was in Wario's car for the Guild job, she watched the blue-clad Luigi smile his way through a compound gate that had no business opening for him, and she was the voice on the crackling phone line saying the thing nobody in the car wanted to say: this is not him. When the fight came, she did not posture. She took an arm, twisted it behind the impostor's back, and kept it there through the headbutt, the broom, and the last chance. Waluigi trusts her grip and her read in that order.

## The Rescue After The Interrogation

Mona's instincts did not stop at identifying the wrong Luigi. In the sequel search she argued that the dangerous lead could not be ignored, called through the lava moat with the others, helped steady Luigi on the way out, and turned toward Star Hill when Jimmy T named the practical need for a hospital. The page should remember that she was not only right about the fraud; she helped get the real man breathing in a clean room.

name: Ashley
title: Witch of the WarioWare Crew
status: Active — scouted the lava-moat tunnels and Star Hill route during Luigi's rescue, 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF
summary: The crew's witch. Said almost nothing at the compound and meant all of it — her two words to the exposed impostor were 'We trusted you,' delivered cold. Worked him over with an enchanted broom, mounted it when he still would not name himself, and took him for the ride that ended with him unconscious, tied up, and out of jokes. The Garden Above the Fire extends Ashley's role from punishment to rescue: she searched from above, found sightlines the ground team lacked, scouted the tunnel exits, and reached the clinic by window because doors remain optional to her.
description:
Waluigi's notes on Ashley from the compound night are short because Ashley was short. She got out of Wario's car, watched the impostor's whole grinning confession without interrupting once, and then went to work with a broom that crackles at the tip when she means it. Three sentences total on the record, four if the last chance counts double: the trust, the threat to the teeth, the ride, the terms. The impostor laughed through Wario and Waluigi both. He stopped laughing when she got on the broom. Waluigi has filed braver men than that impostor and worse fates than unconsciousness, and he ranks the ride somewhere between the two.

## The Search Above The Lava

Ashley saw what the ground team could not: smoke, figures on the high rocks, and later the path ahead through the tunnels. Her broom stopped being an interrogation threat and became rescue equipment. Waluigi files this as a correction to anyone who thinks quiet means uninvolved; Ashley says little because she is already moving.
