name: Jimmy T
title: WarioWare Crew
status: Active — followed the lava-moat rescue to Star Hill clinic and pushed for medical care, 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF
summary: One of Wario's crew. Rode in on the Guild job, got out of the car for the reckoning, and did the quiet work of it: crossed arms, cracked knuckles, and the impostor's second arm yanked the other way while Mona held the first. Asked the only question that mattered at the end of the night — 'And step three?' — and got a plan worth grinning at. The Garden Above the Fire gives Jimmy T the practical question after the rescue: once Luigi was found alive, he was the one who asked about a hospital, turning shock into the next step.
description:
Waluigi barely heard Jimmy T all night, which is why Waluigi remembers everything he did hear. He stepped out of Wario's car with his arms crossed and his attention fixed, took the impostor's free arm when Mona took the first, and leaned down with the whole crew to deliver the night's shortest sentence: 'We're waiting.' Later, outside the walls, while Wario paced and the prisoner lay tied and senseless, Jimmy T asked for step three of the plan and grinned slyly at the answer. Few words, both arms, full attention. Waluigi has worked with louder men and learned less from all of them.

## The Practical Question

Jimmy T's compound-night record now has a second quiet hinge. After crossing the lava rocks badly but loyally, after bringing up the rear out of the tunnel, he asked the question that moved the scene from rescue to treatment: what about getting Luigi to a hospital? It was not dramatic. It was useful, which is rarer.

summary: One of the WarioWare ninja twins. Kat was not part of the compound mission and followed anyway, which Wario called idiotic right up until she reported seeing Luigi alive, burned, limping, and repeating 'find them.'
description: Kat enters the compound-night file from above the lava, which is exactly how Waluigi expects ninjas to enter files he did not ask them to join. name: Ana

summary: One of the WarioWare ninja twins. Ana followed the rescue party with Kat, helped confirm Luigi was alive, and supplied the detail Waluigi needed most before he admitted needing it: Luigi's face had not been burned.
description: Ana's witness statement is short and therefore useful. She saw Luigi moving, saw burns on his arms and legs, and noticed that his face was clear. name: Dr. Toad
title: The Star Hill Physician With the Least Suspicious Name Possible
status: Unknown — his clinic was reported locked down with a 'private wing' on 2 Aethel 1035; the same night a courier went through its front window and something in Luigi's clothes stood outside it; nobody has heard from the doctor since the rest order
affiliation: Dr. Toad's Star Hill Clinic / Mushroom Kingdom medicine
summary: A Star Hill doctor who treated Luigi's burns after the lava-falls rescue, diagnosed pain-and-exhaustion delirium, and prescribed clean dressings, fluids, rest, and no adventuring. Waluigi remains suspicious of the name but not the treatment.
description:
Dr. Toad is, according to Dr. Toad, actually named Dr. Toad. Waluigi asked because somebody had to. The doctor treated Luigi's arm and leg burns as serious but survivable, identified confusion and trauma signs without forcing the Mario question open, and left the room quickly once he understood that the word brother was now a surgical instrument. This file credits him for competent care and an excellent instinct for retreat.

**Backfilled from 2 Aethel, 1035 BF.** Dr. Toad does not appear in the record of the night his clinic became the centre of what a courier called a 'rot-zone'. A helicopter crashed on the storehouse roof next door, a courier went through his front window and came out of the neighbouring stairwell, a mouth opened in the road outside his door, and Mr. L stood in his street in triplicate. The informant's report placed a private wing and a high-security patient upstairs. No staff were seen. The front window is broken. The archive would like to hear from him and has no way of asking.

name: Black
title: Colour Division, Iron Legion Special Forces - the One Who Recognised the Onesie
race: Unrecorded - presents as a man-shaped shadow on command
status: Active - holding the upstairs landing of the Overgrown Manor with Hjumpik's friends in handcuffs
affiliation: The Colour Division / Iron Legion special forces
summary: The fourth of the Colour Division, who turns into a shadow when he introduces himself and who was the one who actually made the identification: nobody else in the manor is wearing a wolf-pelt onesie. He is polite, he is correct, and he is the reason the party's night stopped being about plants.
description:
Four operatives came through the door of a room the house guard had locked, and they introduced themselves in sequence, by colour, with a flourish each. *I'm Red. I'm Green. I'm Yellow.* And the fourth one said *I'm Black*, and became a shadow, and the archive notes that Waluigi opened his mouth to ask a question and then closed it again, which has happened perhaps four times in his recorded life.

Black is the one who did the work. Hjumpik tried the oldest trick available - *I can relay that information to him* - and it very nearly took, because the other three wanted it to. Black looked at the dwarf for slightly too long and said it: *you ARE Hjumpik. You have the signature wolf-pelt onesie on.*

Hjumpik's defence, filed in full because it is the funniest sentence in the session: *you know, a lot of dwarves use this stuff, it's kind of racist, all dwarves use wolf pelt.* It did not work. He closed the door slowly and ran upstairs.

What Black wants is simple and nasty. Hjumpik's mission ran past five nights; the Aegis Magi want their contractor back; the Division was sent to collect. When the dwarf asked for time to investigate, Black granted it - and took Toad Lee and Waluigi as leverage while he was granting it. Handcuffs, not mage cages, and only because Hjumpik put a hand on his warhammer and said *they're not animals*.

The archive files him as reasonable, which in this arc is a threat assessment rather than a compliment.

name: Sensei
title: Advisor to Classroom 2-B / SCHALE Liaison
status: Active — newly assigned advisor to Classroom 2-B at Trinity General School; disclosed the class's SCHALE attachment during his first roll call and opened an internal query into the Equestrian liaison security breach
summary:
Sensei is the advisor assigned to Classroom 2-B, and the first adult in this campaign's record to tell the students what they are actually enrolled in. He introduced himself as the glue holding the operation together, ran a roll call, and — when a student asked a direct question — confirmed that the class is attached to SCHALE operations. He is not the students' friend and does not try to be. He is the person who answers the question.

His method is volume and posture rather than authority he actually possesses. He defused a student's declaration of lordship by thanking him for his cooperation. He is, on the evidence of one session, a man who has run this room before and expects to run it again.
description:
Waluigi has read the transcript twice and wants to be fair to the man, which is not Waluigi's default setting.

## What he did

He walked in, adjusted glasses that the record explicitly notes he does not need for vision, and announced a deal: follow the rules, behave like students, everything goes smoothly. Then he ran a roll call off a clipboard, and the roll call is the spine of the whole filing — it is how eleven people got introduced to each other and to the archive at the same time.

He ate a chocolate a student offered him. He examined it with exaggerated suspicion for three seconds first, then pronounced it *not bad*. That is the single most efficient characterisation in the session: he performs the suspicion, and then he eats the sweet.

## The disclosure

Asked what SCHALE was, he did not deflect. He wrote it out: **Strategic Counter Hazard Activation League Execution.** He conceded, unprompted, that it sounds stupid. Then he explained what it does — Knight deployments, resource allocation, evacuation orders during hazard events — and said the thing that makes the filing matter: *it's the difference between knowing there's a threat and actually doing something about it.*

He also disclosed that the class is part of it. Several students plainly did not know. One of them had been at Trinity for years.

## The two lines that cost him

First: asked about the Equestrian liaisons seen walking the school openly, his jaw tightened and he set the clipboard down. He confirmed a diplomatic programme with Canterlot, confirmed it was meant to be quiet, and said that students seeing it meant *someone dropped the ball on security protocols.* He told the room to report further sightings to him directly — not to social media, not to friends. That is a man containing a breach in real time.

Second, and worse: asked whether the students get guns, he said nobody is handing out guns — and then, preempting an objection nobody had voiced, added *except Tsurugi. You already have clearance.* He disclosed one student's armed status to a room of ten others in order to win an argument he was already winning.

## Waluigi's assessment

He is competent, tired, and honest in the specific way that gets people into trouble: he answers what he is asked. A more careful man would have let the SCHALE question die. A worse man would have lied. Sensei did neither, and as a result eleven children now know what they are in.

**Waluigi's note:** the man promised discipline and scheduling and then briefed a classroom on weapons interdiction in the eastern sectors. Waluigi is not saying he is a liar. Waluigi is saying the job description was written by somebody else. WAH.

name: Kurimura Airi
title: The One With The Chocolate / Classroom 2-B
status: Active — student, Classroom 2-B; founding member of the outfit-design alliance formed during the advisor's first roll call
summary: Airi sits by the window, keeps chocolate in her desk drawer, and is the social connective tissue of Classroom 2-B. She welcomed the new advisor, briefed the newcomer on what was normal, gave the advisor a chocolate mint, then carried another one to the back of the room for the student nobody else was talking to. Her enthusiasm is constant and occasionally deafening, and it is also the only thing in the room that reliably crosses the seating politics.
description:
Waluigi wants to make a case for Airi, because the transcript makes her easy to underestimate and the transcript is wrong.

## What she actually does

Airi asks three questions about snacks and outfits, screams about a fashion show, and balances her chair on two legs. That is the surface. Underneath it, in one session, she: reassured the newcomer that they were in the right room; told them Mika behaves this way with every new teacher so they would not take it personally; gave the advisor a chocolate before he had established anything; walked to the back of the classroom to hand a second chocolate to Shaggy, who had been sitting alone and trying to be invisible; and told Hanae she was a genius the moment Hanae volunteered something.

Every one of those is a person moving toward someone who is isolated. She does it constantly and she does not appear to notice she is doing it.

## The chocolate

Chocolate mint, *the good kind*, produced from a desk drawer and from — the record says — seemingly nowhere. It functions in the filing as a unit of social currency: offered to the advisor as a welcome, offered to Shaggy as company. Waluigi notes that nobody gave Airi anything all session.

## The alliance

When Asa Hanko proposed designing outfits for the class instead of doing paperwork, Airi escalated it to a fashion show within seconds, recruited Hanae by praising her, and then aimed the whole thing at Kenzaki Tsurugi — the least approachable person in the room — announcing they would make everyone look so good that even Tsurugi could not complain. Tsurugi's mouth twitched. Airi screamed with joy.

That is the session's warmest moment and it was engineered, accidentally, by someone who wanted to put balloons on tactical gear.

**Waluigi's note:** Waluigi has been the loud one in a room for eighty years and can tell you precisely how much of it is armour. Airi asked whether the advisor would be around at break. That is not a question about scheduling. WAH.

name: Iochi Mari
title: Sisterhood Club / The One Who Actually Quiets The Room
status: Active — student, Classroom 2-B; Sisterhood Club representative
affiliation: Trinity General School, Classroom 2-B; the Sisterhood Club
summary: Mari is the student who welcomed the advisor formally, offered the Sisterhood Club's help before being asked, and then quietly got the classroom under control when shouting had failed. She sits with good posture, laces her fingers on the desk, and tucks a strand of hair behind her ear before she says anything that matters. She is also the person who translated SCHALE into plain language for the students who were too embarrassed to admit they did not understand it.
description:
## The competence

When the advisor lost the room — chairs scraping, one student spinning on a desk, another delivering a monologue to the fluorescent lights — Mari stood up, walked to the front, positioned herself slightly behind the advisor's desk, and said that if everyone could take their seats that would be wonderful. The record is explicit about what happened next: her voice cut through the noise more effectively than any shouting, and students began complying one by one *like dominoes falling.*

She did not raise her voice. She did not have authority. She simply went and stood at the front and was reasonable, and the room folded.

## The translation

Shaggy admitted he had been at Trinity for a long time and nobody had ever explained any of this to him. Mari turned to him and explained it — patiently, and with the specific grace of opening with *most people don't fully understand it until they're told directly*, which hands the listener a way to not be ashamed. Then she laid out SCHALE in three clean sentences: the system that keeps order, coordinates Knight deployments and Resistance intelligence, translates strategy into actual missions.

She checked her account against the advisor's face while she gave it. She was right.

## The question underneath

When the room had descended into outfit requests and snack negotiations, Mari raised her hand — though she had already been looking at him — and asked the only question in the session that went to the point:

> *"I think what everyone here is actually asking — underneath all the outfit requests and snack searches — is whether SCHALE means we'll get to DO something meaningful. People don't care about gadgets or uniforms. They care about purpose. So… will it?"*

The record does not show the advisor answering it.

## Waluigi's assessment

Mari is the most dangerous person in that classroom and it will take everyone several sessions to notice, because danger in this archive is usually loud. She notices what people are actually asking. She noticed Lord Verity's voice change when SCHALE was mentioned and filed it silently. She leaned over to reassure Yoshimi — who had visibly flinched at her own name — that the theatrical boy was not actually scary.

**Waluigi's note:** the girl calmed a riot by asking nicely and then asked the teacher the one question he could not answer. Waluigi would like it on record that Waluigi spotted her first. WAH.

name: Misono Mika
title: The Princess Of The Front Row
status: Active — student, Classroom 2-B; claimed the desk directly opposite the advisor's on the first day and has not surrendered it
summary: Mika arrived in Classroom 2-B roughly ten seconds before anyone had processed that the door had opened, slammed both palms on the advisor's desk hard enough to rattle the pencil holder, and asked whether getting there first made her his favourite student. She then claimed the desk directly across from his and sat in it with deliberate, princess-like posture. Her halo spins faster when she is excited, which is most of the time.
description:
## The entrance

Pink hair bouncing, skidding to a stop, both palms down on the desk, halo spinning above her head like an excited top. *SENSEI! I got here first! Does that mean I'm your favorite student now~?*

Then she sat down opposite him — prime real estate, claimed before the rest of the class had finished filing in — with her back straight, hands folded, chin slightly elevated. The posture is the tell. She bursts into a room like a thrown object and then arranges herself like she is being painted.

## The tea

The best line in the session and it is hers:

> *"Also I brought you tea! Well… I didn't bring tea. But I* thought *about bringing tea."* A pause. *"…The thought counts."*

That is a complete character study in three sentences. The intention arrives fully formed and beautifully staged; the tea does not exist.

## The pattern

She put her hand up to ask why she had not been called yet, mid-roll-call, having not yet been reached. She ended up sitting on top of her desk rather than in her chair. She spun on the chair for no stated reason. She stopped spinning when SCHALE was mentioned and leaned forward with genuine interest — the record marks this as unusual for her, which means the mention landed.

And once, describing herself, she said: *your princess is ready to serve her prince, obviously. That's just… that's how it works.* Then cleared her throat, smoothed her dress, and tried to look dignified. She had heard herself.

## Waluigi's assessment

Waluigi recognises the shape of this because Waluigi has been doing a version of it for a very long time. Arrive first, arrive loudest, claim the seat nearest the person whose attention is scarce, and frame the whole thing as a joke so that if the attention does not come you were never really asking.

The halo spins faster when she is excited. Nobody in that room has asked her why she needed to be first.

**Waluigi's note:** she thought about bringing tea. Waluigi is filing that under *things that are funnier the third time you read them and slightly sad the fourth.* WAH.
fullBodyCaption: Full-body token plate — Misono Mika head to foot on a transparent field, the look of the lead; cut from a keyed render on 2026-10-05 for the table's token.

name: Shirasu Azusa
title: Supplementary Student / The Corner Desk
status: Active — student, Classroom 2-B; classified within the school system as a supplementary student, a designation she named aloud and objected to
summary: Azusa sits in the far corner, as far from everyone else as a desk allows, with her posture straight, her pen aligned parallel to her notebook's edge, and her expression unreadable. She answers roll call with a nod barely large enough to register. She is also the only student in the room who reacted to the word SCHALE with something other than excitement, because she is the only one who has been on the receiving end of it.
description:
## The corner

Her desk is angled slightly away from the rest of the class — the record compares it to a ship positioned to leave port at a moment's notice. Hands folded. Notebook squared. Pen parallel to the edge. A breeze from a cracked window pushes a strand of hair across her face during roll call and she does not move to fix it.

The stillness is not calm. It is maintained.

## What SCHALE means to her

When the advisor said the word, the room lit up — Lord Verity vibrating, Mika leaning forward, Airi bouncing. Azusa's eyes sharpened, and the record describes it precisely: *like a blade being drawn from a sheath so smooth you'd miss it if you blinked.*

She knows what SCHALE is better than most students at Trinity, because she has seen the other side of it. The record is explicit about her objection: she has felt *the weight of systems that sort people into categories they didn't choose. Into boxes labeled 'supplementary' like it's a diagnosis rather than a circumstance.*

## The line

While the rest of the room negotiated outfits, Azusa asked the question underneath the whole session, quietly, to nobody:

> *"The question is whether SCHALE actually works. Or if it's just another thing that sounds important but doesn't do anything for people who are already at the bottom of every list."*

And then, quieter still:

> *"…Doesn't matter though. I'm not on any list. Supplementary students don't count for much either way."*

Nobody in the classroom responded. The archive is recording that fact deliberately.

## The notebook

Neat margins, colour-coded tabs. When the outfit proposal reached her she wrote two words in small precise handwriting — **CUTE OUTFITS** — and then stared at what she had written as though it had personally offended her. She filed it, in her own phrase, under *waste of time.* She still wrote it down.

Waluigi notes that she is taking minutes of a meeting nobody asked her to minute, in a room she has positioned herself to leave.

**Waluigi's note:** she said supplementary students don't count for much and ELEVEN PEOPLE heard her say it and not one of them said otherwise. Waluigi is filing that silence as the loudest thing in the session. WAH.
fullBodyCaption: Full-body token plate — Shirasu Azusa head to foot on a transparent field, the look of the lead; cut from a keyed render on 2026-10-05 for the table's token.

name: Ibaragi Yoshimi
title: The One Who Finished Page Six
status: Active — student, Classroom 2-B; declined to join the alliance and volunteered to read the documentation instead
summary: Yoshimi sits in the middle row with her arms crossed tight, flinches when her own name is read, and goes red when anyone looks at her directly. Her contribution to the session was to refuse the alliance, refuse group uniforms, and then produce a crumpled SCHALE pamphlet from her bag and announce that she had finished page six — the only student in the room who had done the reading.
description:
## The flinch

The roll call reached her name and the record catches a sharp intake of breath from the middle row. When the advisor glanced up she was hunched in her seat *like she's trying to physically shrink herself smaller*, gripping the desk hard enough to whiten her knuckles. She said *I'm here.* Her eyes scanned the room to see who was watching, landed on the advisor looking directly at her, and she flinched again and looked away fast.

Mari leaned over and told her the theatrical boy was not actually scary. It is the only kindness anyone extends to Yoshimi in the entire session and she does not acknowledge it.

## The refusals

She is a machine for saying no to things she has not been offered.

On outfits: *If this is about uniforms, I'm opting out. I don't do group matching. Last time the school made me wear anything I looked like a kid playing dress-up.*

On the alliance: *An alliance. They're forming an* alliance *over a cape.* Then, flatly: *I'm not joining any alliance.*

And then, immediately, in the same breath — the tell:

> *"But if Sensei needs someone who actually reads the handouts…"*

She slapped a crumpled pamphlet on the desk with more force than necessary. **"I finished page six."**

## What that is

That is an application. Waluigi is going to be very clear about this, because the room read it as contempt and the room was wrong. She refused the alliance, and then in the next sentence offered the one thing she is confident she is good at, to the one person in the room with authority, and made it sound like an insult so that it would not count as asking.

She also hissed at Airi — *How much of what Sensei said are you actually hearing right now?* — while Airi bounced obliviously past. Yoshimi had been listening to every word. It was bothering her that nobody else was.

## The ear

When the advisor announced the deployment rotation, Yoshimi mumbled *boring* under her breath and immediately stared at her desk when he glanced over. The record notes the tip of one ear had gone red, and adds: *She'd be furious if anyone pointed it out.*

**Waluigi's note:** she read the pamphlet. Nobody made her read the pamphlet. She read the pamphlet, brought it to class, and waited the entire session for a reason to mention it. Waluigi knows exactly what that is and will not be saying it out loud where she can hear. WAH.

name: Asagao Hanae
title: Logistics And Scheduling / The Colour-Coded Notebook
status: Active — student, Classroom 2-B; joined the alliance on a logistics remit and is cross-referencing SCHALE documentation against school emergency protocols on her own initiative
summary: Hanae answers roll call in a whisper with her fingers trembling, asks to be taken care of, and spends most of the session pulling her sleeve over her knuckles. She is also, on the evidence of her own notebook, the only person in the building who has independently audited the SCHALE briefing material and found gaps in it.
description:
## The volume

Everything Hanae says is delivered at a volume the record repeatedly describes as barely existing. *I-I'm here… Sensei…* — barely above a whisper. *P-Please take care of me…* — fingers trembling, eyes on the floor, sleeve pulled over the knuckles.

She held the advisor's gaze for exactly two seconds when SCHALE was first mentioned, said *I know what that is*, and then her courage ran out and she looked back down at the desk.

## The notebook

And then, when the alliance formed, she raised her hand hesitantly — the record compares it to asking permission to speak at a town hall — and produced a small notebook filled with neat handwriting and colour-coded tabs, and said this:

> *"I already started organizing the SCHALE information Sensei shared. There were gaps in the documentation so I cross-referenced it with the school's emergency protocols…"*

Nobody asked her to do that. It had been a matter of hours. She found gaps.

She offered logistics and scheduling, apologised for not being able to do capes or speeches, and held the notebook up like proof of qualifications at an interview nobody was conducting.

## The lamp

When Asa Hanko dismissed paperwork and proposed designing cute outfits instead, the obvious outcome was that Hanae would fold. Instead the record says her eyes lit up *like someone just turned on a lamp inside her chest cavity*, and she said *that might actually be fun* — then immediately began volunteering detailed logistical support for an outfit committee that did not yet exist, offering to check uniform modifications against school regulations, and trailed off when she heard herself doing it. Her ears went pink.

Then Airi called her a genius and a hidden treasure and shook her hands, and Hanae looked startled and did not pull away.

## Waluigi's assessment

There is a specific kind of person who is terrified of being perceived and simultaneously desperate to be useful, and who resolves the contradiction by doing enormous amounts of unasked-for work in private and then presenting it, shaking, as an offering. Waluigi has filed a great many of them and they are usually the reason anything functions.

**Waluigi's note:** she found GAPS in the documentation. On day one. While apologising for existing. Somebody give the child a desk and a budget. WAH.

name: Kenzaki Tsurugi
title: The Back Row / Cleared
status: Active — student, Classroom 2-B; the only student in the room disclosed as holding weapons clearance, a fact the advisor announced publicly without her consent
summary: Tsurugi occupies the back row with her arms crossed and her legs on the desk, laughs a low *keheh* at things nobody else finds funny, and watches the advisor rather than the chaos. She is the only student who challenged the idea of arming the class — and the only one the advisor then revealed was already armed.
description:
## The posture

Legs kicked up on the desk, arms crossed, chin angled down, dark hair across one eye. The record describes her eyes as sharp enough to cut glass and her attention as a predator sizing up whether something is worth the effort of killing. She did not raise her hand at roll call. She said *tch*, looked away, and muttered *what a pain.*

When the classroom lost its mind she watched the advisor. Only the advisor. The record is specific about this twice.

## The two words

Her register is short and it lands. *Keheh.* *Tch.* *What a circus.* Asked to comment on the advisor's promise of eventual equipment: *…Not yet, huh. How long do we have to wait? …Days? Weeks?* — two syllables at a time, no filler, no hedging.

And the assessment that should worry him: *You're losing your authority, Sensei. Just so you know.* She was right, and she was the only person in the room tracking it.

## The gun question

When a student asked whether they all get guns, Tsurugi's response was the sharpest thing in the session. She uncrossed her arms slowly, leaned forward, pointed at the advisor, and said that if he was about to say yes then the class was an excuse for a shooting range and she would be filing paperwork. Then:

> *"I've handled weapons since before most of you were old enough to stop putting them in your mouths."*

And: **"Sensei. What's the actual plan?"**

That is a student with weapons experience objecting to arming children. It is the most responsible position anyone takes in the entire filing and it is taken by the girl with her boots on the furniture.

## What the advisor did with it

He said nobody is handing out guns — then held up a finger to preempt an objection she had not made and added *except Tsurugi. You already have clearance.*

He disclosed her armed status to ten classmates to win an argument. She had not volunteered it. The record does not show her reacting, which Waluigi considers the most informative non-reaction in the session.

## The twitch

Airi, planning a fashion show, declared they would make everyone look so good that even Kenzaki could not complain, and proposed balloons on SCHALE tactical gear. Tsurugi stared at her for a long uncomfortable beat. Then, so quietly the record says it almost did not exist, the corner of her mouth twitched. *Keheh.*

**Waluigi's note:** everyone in that room is frightened of her and she is the only one who tried to stop the teacher arming the children. Waluigi will be watching what the school does with a student it has already cleared and already exposed. WAH.

name: Asa Hanko
title: Classroom 2-B / The One Who Kept Asking
status: Active — student, Classroom 2-B; asked the questions that produced the SCHALE disclosure and the Equestrian liaison admission
summary: Asa Hanko is the student the advisor had to look twice at to place, and the one who did the most damage to his lesson plan. Hanko asked what SCHALE was, asked what the acronym actually meant, asked what Sectors 7 through 12 were, asked about the Equestrian liaison seen walking the school, and asked whether the class would be armed. Every significant disclosure in the filing exists because Hanko would not let a term pass unexplained.
description:
## The newcomer's advantage

Hanko spends the first part of the session confused and says so — *what the hell? is this really the right place?* — and that confusion turns out to be the most useful instrument in the room. Everyone else had been at Trinity long enough to nod along at unfamiliar words. Hanko had not, and asked.

The roll call did not help. The advisor read out *Lord Verity*, looked around the room for anyone matching the description, landed on Hanko with an eyebrow raised, and said *Huh. You're Lord Verity? …Alright then.* He checked the box and moved on. It took a second intervention — *sensei what about me!* — for him to find the right line on the clipboard and produce the actual name.

## The questions that moved the session

In order, each one prising open something the class had not been told:

1. **"SCHALE operations?"** — the question that stopped the lesson and made half the room sit up.
2. **"what are you guys talking about? what does any of this mean sensei"** — the honest one, which gave Shaggy cover to admit he had been at Trinity for years without ever having this explained.
3. **"Strategic Counter Hazard Activation League Execution? sounds stupid, what does it actually do?"** — which got the advisor to concede *it does sound stupid* and then explain the function properly.
4. **"Sector 7 through 12? Resistance? what does that mean?"** — which produced the whiteboard map and the advisor's one-line characterisation of the Resistance as *the bad guys.*
5. **The Equestrian question**, below.
6. **"We can all use guns at least right?"** — which produced Tsurugi's objection and the advisor's disclosure of her clearance.

## The Equestrian question

The important one, and Hanko asked it almost in passing:

> *"so we don't deal with external threats only internal what about the pony liaison that came from equestrian earlier i saw some walking around the school was that meant to be private"*

The advisor's jaw tightened. He set the clipboard down. He confirmed a Canterlot diplomatic programme, confirmed it was supposed to be quiet, and admitted someone had dropped the ball on security protocols. Hanko had seen something the school did not intend anyone to see, and said so in a classroom, and the archive now has a filed admission of a security breach because a confused student mentioned ponies.

## The other register

Hanko is not solemn about any of this. Told there might eventually be equipment, Hanko demanded cute clothes and recruited Airi on the spot. Told the session would cover deployment rotation, Hanko said it was boring. Offered paperwork by Hanae, Hanko said *what no eww* and proposed the class design outfits instead — which is how the alliance came to exist at all. Hanko also clapped for the alliance and declared the three of them would be good friends.

## Waluigi's assessment

The archive should be careful not to tidy this into a portrait of a strategist. Hanko was not interrogating the advisor; Hanko was lost, and asked. But *asked* is rarer than it sounds in a room of people managing their own dignity, and the questions arrived in an order that stripped the session down: what is this, what does it mean, where is it, who are we fighting, and are you giving children weapons.

**Waluigi's note:** Waluigi has read a hundred transcripts where nobody asks the obvious question because everybody assumes they are the only one who does not know. This one has a child who asked five times. WAH.

name: Lord Verity
title: Self-Declared Lord And Master Of Classroom 2-B
status: Active — student, Classroom 2-B; stood down from his claim of dominion after a final warning, and reacted to the SCHALE disclosure with undisguised hunger
summary: Lord Verity wears an oversized hoodie as a cape, stands in front of the fluorescent lights so he throws a silhouette, and has twice demanded that the classroom kneel before him. He is also the student whose voice cracked when he learned the class was attached to SCHALE, and who asked — quietly, for once — whether that meant everyone in the room was part of it.
description:
## The performance

He stands on or in front of furniture. He slams a fist into his palm. He positions himself deliberately in front of the light bank so that he is backlit. The hoodie is a cape and the record is generous enough to call it one.

> **"YES I AM LORD VERITY. AND I SHALL BE YOUR MASTER FROM THIS DAY FORWARD — KNEEL BEFORE ME, MORTALS!"**

Stunned silence, one cough, Mika giggling, Airi covering her mouth, and the advisor blinking twice and saying *…Right. Next.* He tried it a second time — *THIS CLASS IS NOW UNDER MY DOMINION!* — with the same result, and a third time demanding order from a room that was ignoring him.

The record notes, with some precision, that he has read exactly three books and felt all of them deeply.

## The deflation

When the warning came that he would be removed, the whole thing came apart in public. His fist was still in the air. The hoodie slid off one shoulder and pooled on the desk *like a deflated balloon.* And he said:

> *"…You can't kick ME out. I'm not even IN anything yet."*

Then stood in the aisle looking, the record says, less like an emperor and more like someone who wandered into the wrong building, and said *Fine* through gritted teeth.

That sentence is the key to him. *I'm not even in anything yet.* The declarations of lordship are what a person does when he has not been given anything to belong to.

## The crack

And then the advisor said SCHALE, and Lord Verity stopped performing. The record is careful here: his eyes snapped to *actual* attention rather than theatrical attention, the dramatic pose melted *like frost in sunlight*, and his fingers tightened on the desk.

> *"Wait. You're saying this class — THIS class — is connected to SCHALE? As in… actual missions? Real-world operations?"*

His voice cracked on *real-world*. Underneath the theatrics, the record says, there was something raw and hungry — *a kid who's been waiting for exactly this his entire life.* He started to say *I thought we were just—*, stopped himself, swallowed, and put the imperious mask back on. The record's verdict: it *doesn't quite fit right anymore.*

Then he stood up slowly, gripped the desk, and asked the real question: *every single person in this room is a part of SCHALE?*

## Waluigi's assessment

Waluigi has spent a career being the loud one nobody invited, and declines to mock this boy. The cape is not the story. The story is a child who announced himself lord of a room because no institution had yet told him he was in anything, and who dropped the entire act the instant one did.

Mari noticed the voice change and filed it. She was the only one.

**Waluigi's note:** *I'm not even IN anything yet.* Waluigi read that line and had to put the transcript down for a minute. WAH.

name: Shaggy
title: Classroom 2-B / The One Nobody Had Briefed
status: Active — student, Classroom 2-B; disclosed that he has attended Trinity for a long time without ever having SCHALE explained to him
summary: Shaggy slouches, crouches behind his desk to avoid roll call, bounces one leg hard enough to vibrate the furniture, and contributes to the session mainly by admitting he does not understand things. That admission is the most valuable thing anyone says: he has been at Trinity for years and nobody ever explained SCHALE to him, which reframes the entire disclosure from a briefing into an indictment.
description:
## The roll call

His name was read into dead silence. The advisor scanned the room and observed that they were either missing Shaggy or he was hiding behind the sleeping student in the back row. A hand rose slowly from behind a desk near the window, where he had been crouched low trying to make himself invisible, and he stood up with his characteristic slouch, green shirt off one shoulder.

> *"Uh… yo. Present. Like, hi."*

His voice cracked on *hi*. He winced internally and ran a hand over his goatee. The record catches all of it.

## The admission

He asked what SCHALE was — *sounds like some kinda… I dunno, video game thing or whatever?* — and then said the thing that matters:

> *"Like… okay, real talk. I've been at Trinity for a while now and nobody EVER explained this stuff to me. I get that there's Knights, I get that there's the Resistance, I even get that there's some kinda war going on — but 'operations?' Like… combat operations? Because if you're telling me I gotta fight something, I need to know where the nearest exit is first."*

Waluigi wants that paragraph read twice. A student of several years' standing at this school did not know what the school was for. He was not being obtuse. Nobody had told him.

## The reasonable objection

After the Equestrian liaison disclosure, while the room was busy being excited, Shaggy said the sensible thing nobody else said:

> *"if we're dealing with bad guys AND ponies showing up uninvited, that's like… two different problems, right?"*

It is correct. The advisor confirmed it was correct and separated the two.

And on the gun question, which he had no part in raising, he put himself on the record immediately and defensively: *I just want it on the record that I said nothing about wanting guns.* He described himself and Scooby as *diplomatic solution kind of guys.*

## The snacks

He is preoccupied with food throughout, produces a quantity of it the record calls impossible, shows the room photographs of absurd spreads arranged with the care of someone who treats meal preparation as high art, and argues that any functioning system needs incentives. He offers Scooby Snacks as his contribution to the mission.

He also accepted Airi's chocolate mint, told her she was way too nice to him, and immediately whispered a question at a volume the record notes was *not remotely quiet enough.* When Airi later volunteered to sit by someone else, he was heard muttering that nobody ever volunteers to hang out with him.

## Waluigi's assessment

The frightened one asking where the exit is has, in Waluigi's long experience, a better survival record than anyone declaring dominion over a classroom. Shaggy's nervousness is not comic relief; it is the only proportionate response to being told, without warning, that your homework is attached to weapons interdiction.

**Waluigi's note:** he asked where the exits were. In a building that just told him it runs hazard operations. He is the only one who asked. WAH.

name: Fawthful
title: The Usurper at Bowser's Gate
status: Historical actor — identified in the 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF Bowser Castle filings; current whereabouts not established
summary: The historical record identifies Fawthful as the commander who turned a compromised Bowser’s Castle into an invasion route. With Mimbus, Cackletta, a dragon, Magikoopas, and defecting Koopa troops in the field, Fawthful treated the throne as a temporary obstacle on the way to ruling the world—or being worshipped by it.
description:
The historical castle assault is the first filing in which Fawthful appears as a commander rather than a name attached to somebody else’s scheme. The operation began with compromised access, used a dragon as a moving terror weapon, and turned the castle’s own garrison into a question Bowser could not answer quickly enough. Fawthful spoke as though conquest and divinity were merely two labels for the same appointment.

The archive keeps Fawthful distinct from the older Fawful record because the assault account uses this name and does not resolve whether it is a new identity, a title, or a deliberate distortion. Mimbus stood beside Fawthful. Cackletta entered the battle. The distinction matters, and the record is not yet kind enough to settle it. WAH.

name: Mimbus
title: The Hand Beside the Usurper
bodyPlan: a Goomba in a suit — one round mushroom-shaped body that is also the head, short arms, two small feet directly under it, no legs
status: Historical actor — present in the 1035 BF false-heir scheme and castle assault; current whereabouts not established
summary: Mimbus is the operative the historical record places beside Fawthful when the false Bowser Jr. performance gave way to an open assault. The record places Mimbus at the junction between deception, internal betrayal, and the claim that the castle could be turned into a throne for somebody else.
description:
Mimbus did not need to shout to be dangerous in this account. Mimbus was present when the castle’s compromise was explained, present when the false heir’s performance was exposed, and present when the assault became a bid for a world-sized crown. The archive will not assign a species or hidden motive the record does not provide. Presence is enough for this historical filing.

Mimbus is not filed as a generic troop. The same figure crossed the seam between the deception and the battle, which makes Mimbus one of the few people who can connect the castle’s theatrical lie to its physical breach.

name: Cackletta
title: The Witch at the Opening of the Battle
status: Historical actor — entered the 1035 BF Bowser Castle crisis as the major battle began; current whereabouts not established
summary: Cackletta is the spellcaster whose historical arrival turned the castle confrontation from a coup into a major battle. Her appearance links the Bowser Castle backfill to the older Beanbean conflicts without making the archive pretend that the earlier record answered every question about her.
description:
Cackletta arrived at the end of the historical throne-room backfill, when Bowser had stopped treating the castle’s strange behaviour as an irritating family incident and started treating it as a war. Her entrance gave Fawthful’s operation a second centre of gravity: the invasion outside and the spellwork inside were no longer separate threats.

The record ends at the beginning of the engagement. Cackletta is therefore filed as a participant in this historical chain, not because the archive has solved her entire history, but because a battle started and she was in it.

name: The Jester (Goomba)
title: The False Heir's Laugh
status: Historical actor — implicated in the 1035 BF false Bowser Jr. session and castle compromise; current whereabouts not established
summary: The Jester is a Goomba who used the shape or role of Bowser Jr. as part of the historical deception that preceded the castle assault. The performance was funny only until Bowser woke up and found that the joke had been used to move a hostile plan inside his walls.
description:
The Jester’s importance is not that a Goomba put on a ridiculous performance. Bowser’s court had survived ridiculous performances before. The importance is that the false Bowser Jr. session occupied Bowser’s attention while the castle’s loyalties, routes, and defenders were being rearranged around him.

The Jester is filed by the role the record gives him because the name is a name in circulation and the species is clear. He was the jester. He was part of the lie. He was present when the lie became a breach.

name: Gabriel / Freddy
title: The Frontman of the Original Five
race: Human child, murdered at the Hurricane Freddy Fazbear's Pizza; spirit bound for decades to the Freddy Fazbear animatronic
status: Released — set free on Night Seven at 1:47 AM on the 21st of Autumn's End, 1038 BF, in the dissipation event the Mages' Guild filed as 'an unexplained but benign release of bound spiritual energy, origin unknown'
affiliation: The original five animatronics of the Hurricane Freddy Fazbear's Pizza (involuntarily) / Fazbear franchise
summary: Gabriel is the child whose spirit was bound to Freddy Fazbear, the lead performer of the original five animatronics at the Hurricane Freddy Fazbear's Pizza — the franchise's crown jewel, and the place where the original five children were murdered. He spent decades on that main stage haunting the night security staff, outlasting the animatronics themselves, until Wario's seven-night tenure ended in the Secret Bunker and thirty years of sustained grief released its hold. The record lists him with two words and no complaints: Released Night Seven.
description:
## The stage

The Hurricane flagship was the largest, most profitable, and most infamous location in the franchise, and its main dining area was built around the stage where Freddy, Bonnie, and Chica performed. By the time Wario arrived to salvage what he had just bought, the animatronics were gone — moved to storage years earlier — but the stage remained, along with the faded murals, the disconnected speaker system, and several hundred plastic chairs. The haunting, the record makes clear, had never needed the hardware.

It was here that the original five children had been murdered, and here that the original animatronics — Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, Foxy, and the Marionette — had spent decades haunting the night security staff. Gabriel is the spirit the record places inside Freddy: the frontman position, held long past any reason to perform.

## The seven nights

Charlie — the Marionette — made the decision on Night One to allow Wario access, and communicated to all the other animatronic spirits across all seven nights. Waluigi suspects she was telling them something between each night; preparing them; helping them understand what the masks being collected meant. Gabriel is not credited with a single distinct incident in the whole seven-night account — the other spirits got the noted beats (Jeremy stopped pursuing on Night Two; Fritz stopped running on Night Four), while Freddy's frontman simply held his place in the record until the end.

Wario, for his part, walked out of the storage room on Night One with the Freddy mask under his arm and entered it in his ledger as: 'Mask: fancy, probably worth something, keep.'

## Night Seven: the release

In the Secret Bunker, Cassidy — the Anchor, the golden suit seated in a chamber at the very back — released her hold after Wario's business advice. Wario's phone rang; it was his mother; he said 'Bye-bye!' and 'have a rotten day,' and walked out of the chamber talking about his restaurant. Behind him, in the record's own words, thirty years of sustained grief released its hold, and five children who had been trapped in mechanical bodies since before most people currently alive in the Midlands were born found something they had been denied their entire afterlife: permission to stop.

The Mages' Guild, monitoring supernatural energy levels across the Midlands, recorded a significant dissipation event at 1:47 AM on the 21st of Autumn's End, 1038 BF, and filed it as 'an unexplained but benign release of bound spiritual energy, origin unknown.'

## Provenance

Every fact in this profile is grounded in The Seven Nights at Fazbear: A Complete Record, which lists Gabriel / Freddy among its participants with the role: Released Night Seven.
waluigiComment: The Guild's documentation still says 'origin unknown.' Waluigi knows the origin. The origin is garlic breath and business advice. WAH.
imageCaption: The record's own archive sheet — the closest thing to a photograph of Freddy's stage that survives.

name: Cosmic Jester
title: The Bite That Was Taken
race: Cosmic entity — scale and nature unrecorded; the archive holds no description of its body, only of the bite
status: At large — the Big Bite is real, the Jesters are scattered, and the Toad God is gathering Star Shards to take more bites out of the Doughnut World
affiliation: The Doughnut World cosmology — the entity whose bite the Toad God's entire premise is built on; referenced throughout the factions record for Disaster Inc. and the Toad God Interview
summary: The Cosmic Jester is the entity that took the Big Bite. In the cosmology revealed during the Toad God Interview of Aethel 12, 1040, the world is not a sphere or a plane but a doughnut — and a bite-sized chunk of it is simply gone, taken by a Cosmic Jester, causing mass depopulation and scattering the Jesters. The hole is real, it is not a metaphor, people fell into it, and the world is smaller now. The Toad God agreed with the Jester's premise — 'He had a point, we should take more bites and get to the jelly filling' — and has been gathering the Star Shards to do exactly that. The Mushroom Kingdom passed a Containment Act in response. Nothing else is documented about the Jester itself: not its face, not its voice, not its game. Waluigi files it under forces that cannot be outsmarted, only survived or consumed.
description:
## The Big Bite

The core revelation of the Toad God Interview, delivered by the Host after reality warping, mouth removal, and one very awkward card game: the world is a doughnut, and a 'Big Bite' has already been taken out of it by a Cosmic Jester. Estalia responded by sending troops to the other side of the doughnut. The bite caused depopulation. The bite created a hole. The hole is literal — people fell into it, people died, and the world is smaller now. It was all over the news, which is the detail the Toad God used to corner Waluigi over his failure to document it in Walupedia.

## The premise

The Toad God agreed with the Jester's reasoning: 'He had a point, we should take more bites and get to the jelly filling.' That agreement is the engine of the current crisis — the Star Shards the Toad God once split because their combined power was cracking reality are now being gathered again, to take more bites. Wario, characteristically, interrupted the existential revelation to negotiate a 'Chief Acquisitions Officer' role in the consumption of the world.

## The Jesters

The record speaks of the Jesters in the plural and the scatter: the bite scattered them, and their game is one of the unnamed possibilities behind the Toad God's parting instruction to 'play the games.' Whose game it is — the Toad God's, the Cosmic Jester's, or the game of existence itself — Waluigi does not know, and this encyclopedia does not pretend otherwise.

## Provenance

This profile is grounded in the factions record for Disaster Inc. — whose era is named for the Cosmic Jester, whose documented wanderings include the Cosmic Jester's Doughnut World, and whose historian Waluigi carries the participant role 'Traumatized by Cosmic Jesters / The Man Who Was Shushed' — and in the event record The Toad God Interview and the Star Shard.
waluigiComment: Waluigi omitted the Big Bite from this encyclopedia out of fear, and a god had to corner him over a card game to admit it. Documenting a literal hole in the world means admitting there are forces that cannot be outsmarted, only survived or consumed. Waluigi is documenting it now. WAH.
imageCaption: The interview where the bite was revealed — the closest thing to a portrait of the Cosmic Jester that survives.

name: Lord Darian Marsh of the Dark Shores
title: The King Who Checked the Seats
status: Active — escaped the break room through the ceiling, said the word that stopped the show, and is now the only witness who has seen the Director's remote
affiliation: The Dark Shores (a province he rules and styles himself king of)
summary: A lord of the Dark Shores who fell out of the sky onto the Nintendo Mania pilot set with his steward and has spent two filings learning the studio's grammar: the exits lie, the applause is recorded, and the building stops when you tell it CUT. Pressed the button, took the rolling pin, ordered the V formation, crawled for the fire alarm, and hid in the alcove to watch the Director pass.
description: Darian arrived wanting proof of the journey and a way home to his province, and got a course in television instead. His instincts are the filing's engine: he watched Luigi before trusting him, stopped short of telling anyone about Evil Mario in the shadows until the room had seen it for itself, and — alone among everyone in the studio — looked at the audience Wario was playing to and counted the empty seats. He calls himself a king, commands paratroopas he has known for four minutes like a man who has drilled them for years, and answers a hallway full of footsteps by stepping into the dark and waiting. The archive's assessment: the studio picked the wrong lord to trap.
imageCaption: Lead plate — the word that stopped the show. Burned hands, a rolling pin, and one production command.

name: Alistair of the Marshkeepers
title: The Steward Who Stopped the Kill Shot
status: Active — hurled the length of a hallway by a cape's wind and back through a window with a flaming pipe, unkillable and unconsulted
affiliation: The Dark Shores — steward to Lord Darian Marsh
summary: Darian's steward, guide, and — by his own admission — a guide who needed reminding to lead. He inventories rooms, boosts his lord into ceilings, and stopped a rolling pin mid-swing on the hunch that the man under it was not the enemy. He was right.
description: Alistair's filing is a study in corrective action. When the plan failed, he surveyed the break room. When his lord went for a killing blow on an unverified target, he grabbed the arm. When the cape's wind took him, he came back through a window with a flaming pipe and burned the tanuki leaf — a plan his own lord described, accurately, as really stupid. He whispers warnings about noise in ducts, shouts the truth at panicking brothers, and charges battered because standing still is not in his order's vocabulary.

affiliation: The Nintendo Mania studio — cast, under a Director
summary: The corrupted Mario who stepped out of the studio's television, wearing a cape of shadowy pixelated feathers and moving like a special effect. Fought to music. Froze at the word CUT. Outlived the show that employed him.
description: Two filings of violence and this account files him as an actor, not a monster — a read the ice form confirmed itself by smirking at. His costume rack: the pixelated feather cape (power source, yanked off by Luigi in a V-formation dive), a tanuki leaf that brought a fox tail and a second, grinning Wario head, a fire form, and an ice body with glowing eyes. He beat the real Mario in the corridors, hurled Alistair down a hallway with cape wind, and took the first honest hit of his career — a rolling pin to the shoulder from the lord of the Dark Shores. After the curtains he stood in the shadows, watched the Director discipline Wario, and pointed one finger at the exit. What he wants is the open question his article exists to hold.

title: The Man Wario Bows To

description: The Director's dossier fits on a cue sheet: he knew the show had gone over better than Wario thought, he knew the results, and he snapped his own cigar in half saying the quiet part out loud. In the hallway, unaware he was watched, he carried a folder and a small remote device with buttons and wires: a control unit for Evil Mario, or the whole studio. name: Paulo
title: The Courier With a Route
affiliation: Unknown dispatcher — a delivery route that runs through Star Hill
status: At large — last seen walking into the dark end of Star Hill's main street reading Waluigi's working notebook, satchel on, pistol discarded
summary: A courier with a satchel, a cheap pistol, a route through Star Hill, and an issued word for what the hill had become. He shot Mr. L first, went through the clinic's front window for it, put a gun to Waluigi's face twice, and left with the one object nobody flew to Star Hill for. He never set the satchel down.
description:
Paulo entered the archive on the night of 2 Aethel, 1035 BF, in the main street outside Dr. Toad's Star Hill Clinic, where two witnesses watched him from a helicopter as he was recited at by a man in Luigi's clothes. He answered the verse with a pistol. The man in green lengthened, the road opened a mouth beside him, and Paulo went through the clinic's front window — and came out of its stairwell twenty minutes later with the pistol, the satchel, and a route he still intended to finish.

Everything the archive knows about him comes from what he said with a gun in his hand. He called the hill 'this rot-zone', flat, like a shift code, with the stress of a man reading a sign he has walked past before. He asked a notebook of burns and verse for 'coordinates'. He said 'I've got a route. You are standing on my route,' and he meant it. He kept the satchel on through a window, a stairwell that would not stay still, and a street with a mouth in it, and he did not open it once.

His pistol jammed twice on the stairs and fired once in the street. The shot took the lip off a fallen rotor blade beside Waluigi's ear and put the archivist down; Wario threw him the notebook unopened; Paulo caught it, said 'smart', and walked away reading it — 'Now let's see what you wrote down here, purple boy.' A corner of one page tore off on a thorn as he passed. He did not notice. He was reading.

The archive's working position is that he did not coin the vocabulary he used. Couriers are issued words with routes. Whoever dispatches through Star Hill, knew what the hill had become, and named a notebook to a courier before he ever saw it, is the lead. Paulo is the man carrying it.
imageCaption: The courier as the lamp caught him: satchel strap across the chest, cap low, the pistol he would later throw. He never put the bag down.

name: John Lee
title: The Ceremonial Guard Who Got Lost in the Right Direction
status: Unknown as of 1040 BF — last on the record at dawn in Efferd, 955 BF, in Fawful's Bean Badge, asking the Mages' Guild for an escort to his son; no later account places him anywhere
affiliation: Peach's Castle — ceremonial guard of the palace (955 BF); father of Toad Lee
summary: A ceremonial guard at Peach's Castle in the last month of the reign: a Toad whose job was to stand next to a lantern and look like the kingdom was fine. On one night in Efferd, 955 BF he jumped four times because the Mario brothers were coming, got lost five times in the right direction, and ended up in the dungeon corridor where a Koopa who was never locked in shook Fawful's hand with the Mages' Guild watching. He is the only witness the archive has to the Arrangement with a voice, and the first man the Chamberlain told the Guild to kill. He left the castle through the drains with a dead Toad's shortsword, a letter that was not addressed to him and the captain's sash on both arms. His son is the Disaster Inc. Toad Lee.
description:
John Lee enters the archive on one night and, so far, leaves it on the same one. Everything below is from the account of that night — the guard's own, in his order — filed as [The Unlocked Cell](#/article/the_unlocked_cell_955_bf). Waluigi was not born in 955 BF and has no second source; the article says so wherever it matters.

## The Post

Ceremonial guard. The palace kept a lantern post on the ceremonial route so that the castle would look guarded from the places the court walked, and John Lee stood it. Lantern in one hand, an issued sword at the hip that the kingdom had chosen for its look, livery pressed. He was good at standing. He was also, by his own account, a huge fan of the Mario brothers — when the word came down the route that they were expected that night to mediate a meeting with 'this toad guy', he jumped four times, straight up, lantern and all, and was questioned by the head guard for it.

He had a small son in the household. The account places the boy — Toad Lee — at the dining-hall table past midnight with the chambermaid Marilyn, and places John Lee in the doorway, not stopping, because a guard who has left his post has no business in a dining hall and a boy with a maid is a boy who is fine.

## The Night

He was lectured by a Toadsworth in a new suit who had the keys to every door and told him to bask in his inferiority. He got lost: the ballroom with its trumpets and marching Toads, a corridor walled with heavy Toads, the dining hall, a hooded figure passing, a tower storage room. Two guards escorted him down to the dungeon, where the cell was unlocked and the prisoner was a Koopa who greeted the door with *so you finally came to free me — oh. It's you.* The escort fell dead beside him. He stood with his lantern while Fawful shook the Koopa's hand — *I HAVE VICTORY* — and three Mages' Guild hoods said the Guild was already in place and would not act yet. Then he ran.

He reached the captain. Bowser reached the hall — *SURPRISE, IT'S ME* — and the captain died in the fire. John Lee took a dead Toad's shortsword, a letter reading *meet me in Fawful's bean shop*, and the captain's sash, which he wound around both forearms. A Guild hood put Bowser down with one small orb and the hall cheered the Guild. The brothers arrived late. John Lee told the hall that the Guild works with Fawful, and the Chamberlain answered — *like a lost dog; a nuisance to the Toads is a nuisance to us; Mages' Guild, dispatch of them* — and a bolt missed him.

Five hours of warp drains under the castle. One Goomba, stomped — the first thing he ever killed. A second ambush out of a pipe. Then Fawful's Bean Badge at dawn, where the Koopa was already waiting, where the Guild told him his son was being taken care of, where Fawful put on a Guild cloak and explained the vacuum shroom, and where John Lee said he wanted to disappear, then said he wanted his son, then asked the people he had just said he did not trust to walk him to the boy. *Are you stupid?* was the answer. The account ends there.

## What the Archive Makes of Him

Waluigi believes John Lee because nobody invents a night in which they get lost five times. He is not a hero in the account; he is a ceremonial guard who kept moving, and the archive has learned to value the kind of witness who did not understand what he was seeing, because that witness has no theory to protect.

Two things are owed to him and neither has been paid. The first is a second account. The second is his son — who, the archive notes, grew up to be the Toad who reads the diary on the shelf while stronger people argue about which door to kick, and who is now listed in this archive under *Liberated Toads / Disaster Inc.* with no father on the page until tonight. The magistrate Toad Lee the Elder, who signed the evacuation order on Highsun 1, shares the family name; whether John Lee is his brother, his cousin, or nothing to him is a question the account does not answer and Waluigi has not guessed.

His kit, for anybody who needs it at a table: a lantern, a dead Toad's shortsword, a captain's scorched sash wound around both arms, a letter, and no armour worth the name. He jumps when he is happy. He gets lost. He goes anyway.
imageCaption: John Lee as the account leaves him: the lantern, the dead Toad's shortsword, the captain's sash wound around both forearms, the livery scorched at the hem. He is looking past the viewer because, by this point in the night, something was always behind him.

name: The Koopa Prisoner
title: The Prisoner Who Was Never Locked In
status: At large as of the last account — at dawn in Efferd, 955 BF, in Fawful's Bean Badge, holding the fat vial; not placed on Highsun 1 or after
affiliation: Unknown employer — worked with Fawful by his own word ('never thought I'd work with a bean'); moved through Peach's Castle and the Mages' Guild's company without being stopped
summary: The prisoner nobody in Peach's Castle would describe to a guard. A Koopa in an unlocked cell, expecting a friend at the door and getting a ceremonial guard with a lantern — *so you finally came to free me — oh. It's you.* He shook Fawful's hand in front of three Mages' Guild hoods, reached Fawful's bean shop before the Toad who crawled five hours through the drains to find it, and admitted there that he had led the escort into the ambush and had himself alerted the castle to Bowser's attack. He holds a fat glass vial that Fawful's plan runs through. Waluigi's working name for him is the Arrangement's courier.
description:
The Koopa has no name in the archive because the account that holds him never got one. He is filed as what he did, which is more than the archive can say for most of the people on the Arrangement's page.

## The Cell

The castle called him a prisoner and withheld his species from its own guards — every Toad on the ceremonial route knew there was a prisoner and not one knew it was a Koopa. The cell was unlocked, not forced: turned by a key and left. He greeted the opening door as a man greets a lift he ordered, and corrected himself when he saw who was in it. *So you finally came to free me — oh. It's you.* The escort beside John Lee was dead within the breath. Fawful came in; the Koopa offered a hand; *never thought I'd work with a bean*, in the only normal voice in the corridor.

## The Shop

He was in Fawful's Bean Badge at dawn, ahead of John Lee, and explained two things without being pressed: that he had led the escort into the ambush, and that he had alerted the castle to Bowser's attack. The second sentence is the one the archive keeps turning over. If the castle knew the Koopa King was coming, then the wall coming in was not the night's surprise — the surprise was that Bowser arrived before the brothers did and asked for Peach with nobody ready to hand her over.

He carries the fat vial — the account's phrase, a glass thing with weight in it — through which Fawful's vacuum shroom is to reach Bowser. He did not use it in the account. He is holding it when the account ends.

## What Waluigi Thinks He Is

A courier. Not a conspirator — conspirators have opinions, and this Koopa has an employer and a schedule. He went where the Arrangement needed a body and was never once stopped by a door, which in Peach's Castle in Efferd 955 is the only credential that mattered. The Loyalists have spent fifteen years asking who held the blade on Highsun 1. Waluigi would settle for knowing who held this Koopa's leash, and has opened a lead on the vial because it is the one object in the account that was built to go into somebody.
imageCaption: The Koopa prisoner as the lantern found him — in a cell whose door was never locked, with the fat vial on a cord. Reconstructed from the account; nobody in 955 BF drew him.

name: The Captain of the Palace Guard (955 BF)
title: The Captain Who Stood Between the Fire and the Stair
status: Deceased — killed by Bowser's fire in the hall of Peach's Castle on a night in Efferd, 955 BF, a month or so before the assassination; his sash left the castle on John Lee's arms
affiliation: Peach's Castle — Captain of the Palace Guard
summary: The head of the palace guard in the last month of the reign, known to the archive from one account and one night. He questioned a ceremonial guard for jumping, was warned by the same guard that the dungeon cell was unlocked and full of hoods, and did not get to answer, because Bowser came through the wall and breathed fire down the hall and the captain was standing between the fire and the stair to the royal apartments. His scorched sash is the one piece of him on the record, wound around both of John Lee's forearms.
description:
No name survives in the account. The guards called him the captain; the ceremonial guard called him the head guard; the archive calls him what the Peach's Castle 955 BF roster calls him and files him with the respect the night did not have time for.

## The Two Conversations

The first was a formality: a ceremonial post was bouncing on the route and the captain came to ask why. The account records the questions as a formality and the answer — the Mario brothers are coming — as the only honest thing anybody said before one became two.

The second was the warning, and it is the reason the archive files him at all. John Lee ran up from the dungeon with the cell unlocked behind him, the prisoner a Koopa, a bean in the corridor, three hoods, an escort dead on the flagstones — and told the captain all of it. Whatever the captain would have done with the only accurate report anybody gave the palace that month, the wall came in before he did it.

## The Death

Bowser's fire, down the hall, at a Toad who did not move. The account does not say the captain was the target; it says he was between the fire and the stair up to the royal apartments, and then there was no captain. John Lee was behind him and lived, and took the sash.

## Why He Matters to the File

Because he is the one officer in Peach's Castle who was told the truth about the dungeon and died before he could act on it, and the next officer to speak in the hall was the Chamberlain telling the Mages' Guild to dispatch of the man who had told it. The capital file's forty-seven-minute gap on Highsun 1 is a gap in a guard rotation. A month earlier the guard had a captain. This is how it stopped having one.
imageCaption: The Captain of the Palace Guard, 955 BF, with the sash John Lee would wind around both forearms an hour later. Reconstructed; the account gives the sash, the hall and the fire, not the face.

name: Marilyn
title: The Maid at the Dining-Hall Table
status: Unknown — last placed at the dining-hall table of Peach's Castle past midnight in Efferd, 955 BF, minding a small boy; the account never sees her again
summary: The only servant the account of the unlocked cell names. At one in the morning, with a kart broadcast audible through the wall, she sat at the long table of the dining hall beside a small Toad boy with a plate in front of him — Toad Lee, the ceremonial guard John Lee's son — and minded him. John Lee saw them from the doorway and did not stop. By dawn the Mages' Guild had the boy and described it as protection. Marilyn is the last person the record places with him before that.
description:
Marilyn is a name, a table and a child. The archive has filed people on less and has never been comfortable doing it.

She was a chambermaid of the household in the last month of the reign. The account that holds her — [The Unlocked Cell](#/article/the_unlocked_cell_955_bf) — gives her one appearance: the dining hall of Peach's Castle, past midnight, the kart race through the wall, a small boy at the long table with a plate, and Marilyn beside him. The boy was John Lee's son. John Lee, a guard who had left his post and was in a room he had no business in, saw his son and his son's minder from the doorway and kept walking, because a boy at a table with a maid is a boy who is fine.

That is the last time the account sees either of them in the castle. Five hours and a dungeon later, in a bean shop, the Mages' Guild told the father that his son was being taken care of and that *Toad Lee won't have to worry about being trafficked in our care.* Nobody mentioned the maid.

Waluigi has filed her because the record of a child's custody should name the last person who had him before the people who shot at his father did. Whether she handed the boy over, had him taken, or was somewhere else entirely by then, the account does not say. A lead is open. It is not a large lead. It is the kind the archive keeps because nobody else will.
imageCaption: Marilyn at the long table past midnight, minding a small boy who is just out of frame. The only servant the account names. Reconstructed from that one sentence.
