name: Jimmy Dobson
title: The Bait With a Button
race: Unfiled — presented himself as a lost traveller; carried a badge
status: Active — fired out of a Koopa airship's cannon into the mouth of GB Mario, 20 Harvestide, 1040 BF; whether he came out is unfiled
affiliation: Unfiled — a badge, a raid plan, and a handler who has not been named
summary: A lost traveller in the Golden Land who was neither lost nor unarmed: a fast-talking, sarcastic bait with a button in his pocket and a Koopa assault already on its way. He copes with fear by being rude, commits to a plan out loud at the worst possible moment, and finished the day by climbing into a cannon and immediately asking to be taken back out.
description:
Jimmy Dobson told the host he had been lost for ages, and the host answered by using his name before he gave it. Everything about the line was a performance except the relief, which was real and was the most honest thing he said all day. He was not lost. He was bait, he knew it, and he had agreed to be early.

**What he is like.** He is a talker who gets rude when he is frightened and funny when he is more frightened than that. The account hands him "I am on your side dumbass" as the line that gets a trapped Koopa Troopa out of the rubble, which is how he says kind things: sideways, as an insult, with his hand already on the man's arm. He mimics the host's accent exactly once, to say *okay letsa go*, and he does it the way a man tries on a hat he does not intend to buy; it is a decision wearing a joke. He lies fast and badly ("uhh no") and tells the truth slowly and well. He narrates his own plan out loud at the worst moment ("it's... it's working, I think") because saying it is how he checks it. He gives orders in the voice of someone in command whether or not anyone has put him in command: *deploy the anchor!*, *fire up to him, I'll put an end to this*.

**What he notices.** More than he lets on. He clocked the hand on his shoulder, the use of *Jim*, the shine on the grass, and the fact that the host was grey; he held the last one for two hours because asking would have ended the walk, and asked it the moment the walk stopped mattering. He keeps his worry in his right pocket: squeezing the button is his tell, and the host never once asked what it was, which is the only evidence in the account that the host already knew.

**What he does.** He believes in the plan more than in the people carrying it, and he is the last man aboard Bowser's airship to learn that the plan has more authors than passengers. When a monster asks him *did you want a hero, Jim?* he does not answer. When the monster comes for the ship he picks up the cannonball, climbs into the cannon with it, and says, in order: *I'll put an end to this*, *oof, this was a bad idea*, and *put me back out, put me back out, aaaa*. He is brave in the way impulsive people are brave, which is all at once and with an immediate wish to be a different person.

His badge has no issuer anyone has read. It opened the one door in the account that needed opening, and it is the only piece of paper he carried that he showed to anyone.
waluigiComment: A man who tells you he is lost while holding a detonator is not lost. He is early. He is also, I am sorry to say, the only person in the file who tried to carry a Koopa out of a collapsing building without being asked.
imageCaption: Jimmy Dobson as the account holds him: bomber jacket, right fist locked on the thing in his pocket, badge up in the other hand, and a look that says he has been told this will work.
aliases: Jim (the host's name for him, unasked); the bait; the lodger (Waluigi's, after the cannon)

name: GB Mario
title: The Host Who Knew Your Name
race: Unfiled — a Mario in grey, by his own account "a memory"; became something with one eye
status: Active — last seen with a lodger in his throat and a hand the size of a cloud
affiliation: The Golden Land — host to the King; later, by his own telling, no one's
summary: The friendly stranger who meets travellers on the Golden Land's road: the cap, the glove, the accent leaned on like a doorframe. Black and white under the shine, he says the colours only happen for those who belong in the frame — then grows a single eye, plays Bowser's Koopa Troop like a toy, and finishes by telling the sky the story is not over yet.
description:
Waluigi files him as GB Mario because the account arrives under those letters and nobody in it says what they stand for. He is not the Mario the archive has been looking for. He is not Evil Mario, the cape-wearing actor, nor Director Mario, the cold copy with the remote. He is a third: a Mario who introduces himself before he is asked, uses a visitor's name before he is told, and keeps a smile on his face a heartbeat longer than the mouth under it.

He is also the only Mario on file who tells the truth when someone asks the right question. Asked why he is black and white, he says the place is not real and the colours belong to those inside the frame. Asked if he is really Mario, he says: *mario is... well, mario is a memory.* Then the question he puts back — *are you really anything at all if you're just looking for a villain to hate?* — is as close to an identity statement as the file has. Whatever he is, he tore through a Koopa army, an invulnerable king and a flying fortress in one afternoon, and when it was over he leaned out of the sky and called for the one man who had climbed into a cannon to meet him.
aliases: Mario; "the director making a final edit" (his words); the monster that was Mario
waluigiComment: Three Marios, three directions of travel, and all three of them walk off a set. I have stopped saying 'the Mario file'. It is a casting folder.

name: The King of the Golden Land
title: The Light on the Throne
race: Unfiled — a mountainous silhouette on a throne of light
status: Extinguished — the light went out; nothing was seen to replace it
summary: A giant shape on a throne so bright his features cannot be made out, who asked his host whether this was the traveller he had promised, shook the ceiling with his voice, and fought off a Koopa army and a monster at once before his own light snapped like glass.
description:
The King's voice came in capitals and in the chest. The temperature in the throne room rose when he settled his gaze on a guest, and the ceiling rippled when he said a word. He asked for a traveller. He took the sound of a button for an insult, a Koopa car for a stain, and the monster that had been his host for "an error in the fabric of this world". He is the only one in the account to say that out loud, and it is the closest thing to a rule of the place anyone states.

The light that came off him lit corridors, melted stone, and threw invaders backward by the dozen. It also passed through the monster as though through paper. When it finally broke the sound was glass. Afterwards a Koopa soldier in a service tunnel asked why the light had gone out. Nobody answered him.
waluigiComment: A king who asks 'is this the traveller you promised' has put a host in charge of the door and the door in charge of the king. That is not a throne. That is a hand puppet's hand.

name: Mr. T
title: The Courier Who Cleans the Laundry
status: Active — followed Wario and the Contract of Accord into the Star Hill corridor on 3 Aethel, 1035 BF after watching Beta Luigi walk out with an Archive Hall volume
affiliation: Wario's Enterprise / Waluigi's Audit Desk (Courier & Back-Room Cleaner)
imageCaption: Mr. T in courier trench coat and satchel strap at the Archive Hall table, 3 Aethel, 1035 BF — spectacles fogged, ink under the nails, already having flagged the discrepancy months earlier.
summary: A gaunt, exhausted courier and back-room bookkeeper who writes Wario's daily reports, cleans Waluigi's financial laundry, and knows too much about both men's gambling debts. He slid Waluigi the 'Wario Bowser / Wawario' lyric sheet, fell asleep beneath the Archive Hall's leaking vault, pulled Wario's real backup ledgers off the shelf at random, and proved he had flagged the Treasury of Wonders discrepancy months earlier with 'AUDIT REQUIRED - WARIO' in the corner.
description:
Every crooked enterprise eventually hires one person whose job is to read the pages the principals refuse to open, carry the parcels nobody wants signed for, and keep quiet when the numbers come back wrong. Between Wario's Enterprise and Waluigi's private schemes, that person is Mr. T.

**Role and temperament.** Dry, chronically underslept, and completely unimpressed by his employers' theatrics. He opens the night of 3 Aethel, 1035 BF by sliding a transcribed song sheet across the Archive Hall table to Waluigi — *"Mario, Luigi, Wario, Waluigi, Bowser, and Wario Bowser"* — and pressing him deadpan on whether *Wawaluigi* has two *Wa*s until Waluigi blacks out his own name and walks out into the rain. Left alone under a leaking stone ceiling, Mr. T calls the dripping water *"like music,"* puts his head in his hands, and sleeps straight through until Wario wakes him.

**What he proved at the shelves.** While Wario raged for three hours over forged morning schedules off by nearly ten thousand gold, Mr. T walked to the Archive Hall shelves and plucked *The Complete Ledger of Wario's Enterprise* and its duplicate backup record at random, exposing a fabricated 5,000-gold withdrawal from the Treasury of Wonders. When Wario panicked at a joke about calling the Toad Police Force, Mr. T reminded him calmly that he cleans their dirty laundry for a living — and turned straight to the bottom-left margin of the altered page, where his own warning scribble (*"AUDIT REQUIRED - WARIO"*) had sat unread for months.

**Cross-file identification ('skinny T').** On the preceding night outside Dr. Toad's clinic (*The Rot-Zone at Star Hill*, 2 Aethel, 1035 BF), syndicate courier Paulo mistook the lanky green silhouette in the dark for an acquaintance and spat, *"I didn't know skinny T wore green."* Wario's closing words to Mr. T in the corridor twenty-four hours later — calling him *"a courier who knows too much about gambling debts"* — put a real courier with a single-letter handle inside the exact Star Hill circuit.

name: Beta Luigi
title: The Brother Left Alone
status: Active — walked out of the Archive Hall alone on 3 Aethel, 1035 BF carrying an unnamed volume pulled from the shelves after swearing to make them atone alone
affiliation: None — formerly beside Mario; now acting strictly alone
imageCaption: Beta Luigi at the Archive Hall threshold, 3 Aethel, 1035 BF: cap pulled over hollow, sleepless eyes, tool belt slung across one shoulder, seconds before crushing a live Fire Flower underfoot.
summary: A hollow-eyed, grief-wrecked figure in stained green overalls, heavy tool belt, and low-pulled cap who entered the Archive Hall during a thunderstorm as the third haunting of the week. Followed by a singing chorus of ghosts, a fifteen-foot angry crimson phantom, and Mario's disembodied voice answering in Italian ('Ti perdono. Vai avanti'), he crushed a working Fire Flower under his boot, wept out the whole of 'Alone' on the stone floor, took one book from the shelf, and walked out by himself.
description:
Waluigi refuses to file him cleanly under *Luigi* or under *Mr. L*, because neither entry holds him. The clinic report from the night before puts the Mushroom Kingdom's Luigi in a high-security private wing with his consciousness fluxing; Mr. L stood outside that same building in three grinning copies reciting verses of murder about a brother on a lava bridge. Beta Luigi walked through the Archive Hall door twenty-four hours later carrying the exact opposite wound: not rage at Mario, but unbearable guilt that his own cowardice killed Mario when King Boo took him.

**Appearance.** Stained green work overalls, a heavy leather tool belt pulled over one shoulder, work boots that scrape across the flags, and a dark green cap tugged low enough to swallow his upper face. When he finally looks up, dreadful bruised bags hang beneath barely open eyes and his whole face droops like wax left near a stove.

**What entered with him.** Thunder broke outside the instant the ghosts ringed him at the doorway chanting *"Fell up high to rock bottom..."* He carried a live, working Fire Flower into the room, held it up while humming about failing his big brother, plucked it, dropped it to the wet stone, and crushed it flat under his boot right in front of Waluigi. When Wario and Waluigi tried to reach him, a solid ghostly barrier locked them back while a fifteen-foot angry crimson spirit with tree-trunk arms reared over him — followed by a faint, unmistakable voice answering his sobs in English and Italian: *"Luigi, where did you go? Ti perdono. Vai avanti... Mostra loro che sei il fratello di Mario! Sei Luigi!"*

**Departure.** When the voices cut off at once, he collapsed to the stone, rose again whispering *"they laugh at me, but I'll make them atone, and this time I'll be sure to do it alone,"* pulled a book straight off the physical shelf — proving he was solid enough to take archive property with him — and walked out before anyone could follow.
